stories.Headline: Chile and OpenAI sign deal to explore AI training for civil servants and startup support
stories.Summary:
Chile’s government and OpenAI signed a memorandum of understanding to explore AI training for civil servants and technical support for local startups, OpenAI announced on November 17, 2026. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Ximena Lincolao, Chile’s Minister of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation, signed the agreement on the sidelines of Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World conference in California. The partnership was launched as OpenAI for Chile, part of OpenAI for Countries, and is supported by the U.S. Department of Commerce’s American SI Exports Program, of which OpenAI is an anchor partner. The agreement covers practical training for government staff, potential uses of AI in ministry administration and support for Chilean startups developing their own applications. The memorandum makes no investment or purchasing commitment.

The partners are considering workshops tailored to different government roles, with proposed topics including how to use AI tools effectively, check what they produce and handle sensitive information. The training would also cover when staff need to review an output or make a decision themselves, and one option is to train government staff who could then teach colleagues. A separate part of the agreement would examine where AI might be used in the science ministry’s own administrative processes, with OpenAI potentially advising staff on adopting new models and training them to use the tools. The startup strand would explore access to OpenAI programs and technology, alongside practical training, technical guidance and mentoring, and the partners are also considering ways to connect entrepreneurs with universities and public institutions. A joint task force of ministry and OpenAI representatives is expected to draw up the first work plan, with a remit including choosing priorities, assigning a lead for each activity and setting milestones and measures of success.

George Osborne, Head of OpenAI for Countries, wrote on LinkedIn that through OpenAI for Countries the aim is to help Chile bring AI into public services, equip civil servants with the skills to use it effectively and support entrepreneurs building the next generation of businesses. Osborne also wrote that what is built with Chile can help light the way for others across the region, presenting the agreement as part of OpenAI’s wider work in Latin America. Sam Altman said artificial intelligence is going to be one of the most important ways people’s lives are made better, from accelerating scientific discovery to helping people build things not yet imagined. Altman said he was excited to work with Chile to help public servants use these tools, improve public services and support entrepreneurs building new companies, and to see Chilean startups solve some of the most important problems in the world. Ximena Lincolao said the collaboration would open extraordinary opportunities for scientific discovery, entrepreneurship and innovation across Chile, and that it is about empowering Chileans to push the boundaries of what is possible.

The ministry and OpenAI will agree the activities, eligibility, resources and technology access separately, with privacy and information security safeguards applying to any work that proceeds. Activities will be subject to appropriate safeguards for privacy, information security and responsible use. The training explored in the OpenAI agreement is aimed at government staff, while Chile’s national plan also covers education and research, with the ministry listing resources for teachers and students, courses on AI in teaching and work to make open data available for AI projects. Cooperation could connect entrepreneurs with public institutions, universities and other local partners to develop applications that support Chile’s economic development and public-service priorities. The agreement builds on Chile’s National AI Policy, which already includes AI and ethics training for public officials.

Chile’s National AI Policy and action plan support talent development, research and responsible adoption, and its action plan brings together 177 initiatives coordinated by 14 ministries. In April 2025, the science ministry reported that 78% of those initiatives were underway or complete. OpenAI for Chile is part of OpenAI for Countries, a global initiative to help countries use AI to advance their national priorities, strengthen their economies and expand opportunity. OpenAI works with governments and local partners to turn AI’s potential into practical benefits for their people. The partnership is led by the Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation.

A joint task force is expected to agree priorities and an initial workplan, with leads, milestones and measures of success for each activity. Specific activities, eligibility, resources and access to technology will be agreed separately. The memorandum sets no investment or purchasing commitment. The articles do not state when the first work plan will be completed or which activities will be chosen first. The articles do not state the value of any resources or technology access to be agreed.

Soket AI, an Indian artificial intelligence startup, raised $4 million, around ₹37 crore, from Bajaj Finserv's Finserv Intelligence and Pennant Technologies, TechGig reported on November 19, 2026. Bajaj Finance invested approximately $2 million in the startup, while Pennant Technologies, an investee company of Bajaj Finance, invested another $2 million in the round. Inc42 reported the funding on November 18, 2026, describing it as $4 million, around ₹37 crore, from the same two investors. The startup is building indigenous foundation models focused on mathematics, coding and reasoning, according to Inc42. Soket AI recently launched EKA-1, a 26-billion-parameter foundation model, under Project EKA, its flagship sovereign AI initiative.

The funding will support the startup in scaling its foundation model research and developing AI systems for financial services, cybersecurity, defence and enterprise technology. The $4 million investment will also support applied AI research and enterprise deployments, particularly across financial services, cybersecurity, defence and enterprise technology. The strategic investment is expected to open opportunities for applied AI research, enterprise applications and capability building. It aims to combine Bajaj Finance's industry expertise with Soket AI's foundational research capabilities. Soket AI, founded in 2019 by Abhishek Upperwal, is building a sovereign open-source AI stack that serves a gamut of Indian languages.

Rajeev Jain, Vice Chairman and MD of Bajaj Finance, said the company looks forward to enabling India's indigenous AI ecosystem with Soket AI. Jain said Bajaj Finance looks forward to engaging with frontier research at an early stage. He said the company will bring its scale and domain expertise to turn this research into practical solutions. The strategic investment is expected to facilitate applied AI research and enterprise deployments across financial services, cybersecurity, defence and enterprise technology. The collaboration seeks to open opportunities for applied AI research and capability building.

Soket AI is among a limited set of Indian AI startups developing indigenous foundation models with support from the IndiaAI Mission. Earlier this month, ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations launched Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B, two open-source multilingual models supporting English and 10 Indian languages. Unlike Soket's reasoning-focused EKA-1, ZenteiQ's models are designed as lightweight AI assistants that can run on-premises and on edge devices, including smartphones, without requiring continuous cloud connectivity. AI unicorn Sarvam AI has also expanded its model portfolio with the launch of Prism, an open-weight decision model built on its Sarvam 105B model. The model is designed for enterprise workflows such as customer support routing, security checks and evaluating AI agent activity.

Project EKA, Soket AI's flagship sovereign AI initiative, is backed by the government's IndiaAI Mission. Speaking to Inc42 earlier this year, the founder said the idea is to crack the AI model for India first. stories.Headline: OpenAI researchers report critical PHP flaws that attackers exploit before fixes
stories.Summary:
On August 11, 2026, researchers from OpenAI privately reported critical security vulnerabilities in PHP, a foundational technology powering millions of websites including those built on WordPress and Drupal. Attackers exploited these critical AI-identified PHP vulnerabilities before fixes were publicly released, targeting operational websites and critical systems supporting businesses, government agencies, and essential public services. Reported attacks included the theft of credentials and security keys, unauthorized access to vulnerable servers, and the installation of persistent malware. Attackers also conducted destructive file-wiping and caused permanent loss of critical data, and security researchers reported millions of malicious probes and attempted exploits worldwide. Research published on November 12, 2026, confirmed that attackers exploited the PHP vulnerabilities to compromise production security gateways, install persistent malware, move into internal infrastructure, and conduct destructive attacks against victims.

One principal set of related fixes to PHP to address these AI-discovered defects changed 423 files, adding 11,556 lines and removing 1,017. Developers spent more than two months developing and testing fixes for these vulnerabilities, and attackers began exploiting the weaknesses before the fixes were released, with attacks continuing afterward. Emergency patching creates multiple obligations including eliminating the vulnerability and confirming that the service still works, and questions arose about whether critical user functions were tested and whether the many PHP extensions were tested with the proposed changes. Soon after the fixes were released, a verified crash resulted in new corrections. The available evidence indicates that PHP's automated regression tests are primarily designed, developed, and maintained by members of the open-source development community rather than by a separate, independent professional software testing organization.

The Software Development Technologies Board (SDT Corp) has committed to raising awareness of the urgent need for independent professional software testing and providing financial support to establish the Professional Independent Testing (PIT) Initiative. The mission of PIT is to strengthen the quality of critical open-source technologies by establishing independent professional testing teams, led by experienced Test Managers and Test Architects, with dedicated professional Test Designers and Test Automation Engineers responsible for developing comprehensive, risk-based automated regression test libraries. Ed Kit, author of "Software Testing in the Real World" and CEO at Software Development Technologies, wrote that developers and professional testers bring distinct but complementary expertise, and that believing in your implementation influences what you think to test. He proposed that for significant changes to foundational open-source software, an independent professional testing capability be established, bringing experienced professional testers in early to challenge requirements and design assumptions. He suggested documenting and making public what was tested, what was not, and which risks remain before a release decision, and said one possible discussion point is investing $1 in independent testing for every $2, $3 spent on open-source development.

Kit wrote that he recognized the PHP developers who added automated checks, used continuous integration and sanitizer builds, and worked with outside security specialists, but that he had not found a comprehensive public, independently authored professional QA assessment of the broader release risks. He said there is no publicly established evidence of a dedicated, independent team of professional test engineers responsible for test design and challenging developers' assumptions. He asked who independently evaluates the quality of foundational open-source software supporting businesses, hospitals, banks, governments, airports, space, and much of the internet, naming Linux, OpenSSL, Apache, Python, and PostgreSQL among widely used projects. He said corporate beneficiaries of open source could support shared testing teams through foundations, grants, and sponsorships, and that AI companies should also contribute. The PHP Foundation describes its primary mission as funding PHP developers rather than maintaining a separate professional testing organization, which Kit called fine but said another capability is needed to become the independent professional testing organization.

Kit wrote that he began his career developing software at Bell Laboratories and later worked at Tandem Computers, where he knew extraordinary developers and also saw extraordinary defects created by extraordinary developers, and occasionally was the developer himself. He said he has long advocated Keyword Driven test automation because it separates the work of designing meaningful tests from implementing and executing them. He said AI can now generate code at extraordinary speed, which makes designing the right tests more important, not less, and that developers, test designers, and test automation professionals are not competitors because critical software needs all three. He said testing is risk management, that we can never test every combination of all possible feature variations, but that professional testers should intelligently select the best combinations most likely to reveal the most significant failures. He said that without an independent professional software testing organization there is no dedicated Test Manager to lead and coordinate the testing effort, no independent Test Architect responsible for designing and maintaining a comprehensive test automation framework, and no separate team of professional test designers systematically identifying what needs to be tested.

Kit wrote that we can debate the value of AI discoveries without a coordinated plan to fix vulnerabilities before attackers exploit them, but that the larger concern is dependence on foundational open-source software without sufficient assurance of comprehensive, independent professional testing. He said the PHP vulnerability is much bigger than PHP. The plan is to establish PIT as a private operating foundation and use Open Collective to help launch the initiative, and Kit said this would complement, not replace, the work of developers and security researchers, and that it needs funding. He wrote that AI finds vulnerabilities, developers fix them, and independent professional verification and validation deserve equal attention. The articles leave open whether PIT has been established, who will fund it beyond the stated commitments, and what the outcome of the new corrections after the verified crash will be.

stories.Headline: Microsoft makes Perception generally available to coordinate AI security agents
stories.Summary:
Microsoft announced on November 17, 2026 that Perception, its platform for coordinating AI agents in security work, is now generally available, and TechGig reported the news on November 19, 2026. The product was first shown as Project Perception in July and had been in public preview inside Microsoft Defender since August. Perception directs agents split into red, blue and green teams through playbooks, with red agents probing for weaknesses as attackers, blue agents handling detection and investigations, and green agents fixing problems. Four blue team agents are now generally available: alert triage, attack investigation, detection authoring and threat intelligence. The Recon Agent, a red team component, and Posture Prioritization, a green team agent, are also generally available.

Microsoft said the Alert Triage Agent can manage approximately 80 per cent of alerts in a typical Defender queue, based on an analysis of eight million alerts across its security products. A Web App Pen Test Agent for red teams and a Risk Reduction Agent for green teams have entered preview, and the Risk Reduction Agent can suggest vulnerability shielding when immediate fixes are unavailable. Microsoft is previewing integrations that link Perception to SIEM, SOAR and IT service management tools via MCP and APIs. Agent 365 and Entra Suite, in preview, can detect 60 types of local AI agents, including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and GitHub Copilot, and Intune policies can keep supported agents on devices. In preview in January 2027, new AI Readiness Initiatives in Perception turn Secure Now guidance into actionable plans with shared progress tracking.

Aleš Holeček, president and chief architect of Microsoft Security, wrote that teams set the guardrails and sign off on high-impact actions, and that automated triggers launch playbooks when an incident meets criteria the customer sets. He wrote that a year ago finding a serious, exploitable vulnerability was slow and expensive work done by elite researchers, and that this is no longer true. He wrote that over the past 12 months frontier AI models have become remarkably good at discovering and exploiting software vulnerabilities, and that similar capability is quickly becoming available in open weights models with limited cyber guardrails. He wrote that attacks once requiring specialized resources are now within reach of almost anyone, and that AI has moved from assisting attackers to executing their tasks to planning and running entire campaigns on its own. He wrote that agents are the new insiders, not inherently malicious but performing tasks at machine speed around the clock with broad access to data, apps, tools and other agents, and that like any insider they can make mistakes, be manipulated or be compromised.

Holeček wrote that in a single week this fall PHP disclosed two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities, flaws letting an attacker take control of a server with a single request over the internet. He wrote that at disclosure tens of millions of internet-facing PHP services were running affected versions, and that nearly two weeks later about 29 million services remained vulnerable, with banks, healthcare providers, energy companies and much of the infrastructure the internet runs on behind those servers. He wrote that the same day brought five other major disclosures across the industry, and that within roughly a day of PHP2Shell's disclosure researchers had developed a working, weaponized exploit, expanding the following week to additional PHP versions and configurations. He wrote that the time from discovery to exploit is shrinking from months to minutes, and that attackers can now find and exploit gaps faster than defenders can close them. He wrote that the Microsoft cyber stack has three layers, signals, sensors and actuators, powered by Defender, Entra, Intune, Purview, Sentinel, the network, the operating system, the browser and the hyperscale cloud, connected to the wider ecosystem through more than 500 connectors.

Holeček wrote that Microsoft and partner sources produce more than 165 trillion signals a day, and that a context layer organizes them with each customer's environment into agent-ready, real-time understanding of the digital estate. He wrote that on top sit specialized security agents working as teams through playbooks, directed by a harness and a multi-model approach using the right model for each task. He wrote that new cost management dashboards and a cost estimator help track AI usage, forecast spending and connect costs to measurable security outcomes. He wrote that Integrated Security Operations Center in Defender is generally available for core capabilities, bringing SIEM, user and entity behavior analytics, threat intelligence and threat protection and disruption together, and that eligible Defender Suite, Microsoft 365 E5 and Microsoft 365 E7 customers receive all Sentinel SIEM features, 90-day default data retention for Defender data, more than 500 connectors, reduced ingestion rates and a built-in data lake. He wrote that in 2026 more than 96,000 vulnerabilities have been published to the CVE Program, more than double 2024's roughly 40,000 and more than 20 times the level of 2010, driven in part by AI-assisted vulnerability discovery tools, yet only 26% of vulnerabilities in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog were remediated in 2025.

Holeček wrote that two new playbooks bring together green team agents, including the Posture Prioritization Agent, now generally available, and the Risk Reduction Agent, now in public preview, with coverage spanning Microsoft, Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud. He wrote that vulnerability shielding, available in preview, helps protect vulnerable assets by applying targeted, temporary protection to buy defenders time before a permanent patch, and that during an active attack it can include adjustments to network accessibility and permissions in supported scenarios. He wrote that enhanced data classification in Purview is generally available in January 2027, and that also entering preview in January are grounding protection for Copilot based on sensitive information types and expanded data loss prevention controls for prompts to Copilot and local agents running on Windows. He wrote that the complete breadth of SIEM capabilities is now in preview, and that Perception is built to help security teams move at machine speed, drive outcomes rather than tasks, and automate while staying in control. He wrote that what Microsoft built for humans does not scale for AI, and that the physics of cybersecurity are changing fast.

stories.Headline: Investors buy Anthropic IPO as tech stocks and chipmakers face a broad sell-off
stories.Summary:
Investors piled into the Anthropic initial public offering on Thursday, November 20, 2026, while other technology stocks suffered a broad sell-off. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2 percent, and the S&P 500 logged another ugly day of trading. Chipmakers Nvidia and AMD took hits as selling pressure extended into Friday. Brian Sozzi described this market situation as a perfect storm for the artificial intelligence trade. The IPO featured the brother and sister duo of Dario and Daniela Amade.

The Nasdaq Composite closed at 23,020.97, while the S&P 500 fell to 7,021.68 and the Dow 30 dropped to 48,769.04. Nvidia shares fell to 135.32, and AMD also faced losses alongside a damaging short seller report. CoreWeave reported nearly 90 billion dollars in debt and liabilities with a 709 million dollar third quarter loss. Nvidia reported 116 billion dollars in third quarter revenue, 65 billion dollars in income, and 118 billion dollars in liabilities. The company also holds 32 billion dollars in debt.

Brian Sozzi stated that the Democratic Blue Wave has Wall Street questioning if Washington will brake AI and data center construction. He noted that the market dislikes interim CEO Collect Crest and lacks a timeline for a permanent Nvidia leader. Sozzi mentioned that technical selling events are forcing investors to raise cash during this period. He also cited sticky inflation, hawkish Federal Reserve rhetoric, and tighter financial conditions as contributing factors. He believes the AI trade is being repriced in real time.

Hyperscalers including Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle are no longer cash-flow positive due to massive infrastructure spending. Neoclouds are tens of billions in debt, with CoreWeave seeing its stock price drop over 50 percent recently. Bethany McLean questioned if the hundreds of billions spent on data centers can be repaid when due. Insurance companies and Wall Street hold much of the debt that Nvidia guaranteed. Investors still want an AI future but are less willing to pay any price.

Nvidia previously operated an open checkbook policy under former CEO Jensen Huang to loan money to the neoclouds. These neoclouds used the loans to buy Nvidia chips, a tactic that critics call circular financing. This arrangement made Nvidia the guarantor of last resort for the debt of these newer companies. The AI revolution relied on Nvidia semiconductors as the beating heart of the entire industry build-out. This aggressive financial practice supported the rapid construction of global data centers.

The market remains uncertain about when Nvidia will announce a permanent chief executive officer to replace Jensen Huang. Regulatory fears regarding China have returned to the center of the semiconductor trade, adding further instability. Investors are now weighing the impact of the Democratic wave on aggressive industry financial practices. It remains open whether the AI bubble will burst and who will be left holding the debt. The disconnect persists between the Anthropic sensation and the broader tech sell-off.

stories.Headline: AI companions could help reduce loneliness, study finds
stories.Summary:
Researchers at Durham University Business School have published a study suggesting that AI companions could help reduce loneliness by creating a greater sense of belonging and improving self-esteem among the people who use them. The research was led by associate professor Varqa Shamsi Bahar alongside colleagues from Cardiff University and The University of Manchester, and it appeared in the journal Psychology & Marketing in 2026. The team explored why some AI companions appear to help people feel less lonely, and they introduced the concept of synthetic mindfulness to describe the experience of an AI companion that seems attentive, nonjudgmental and responsive to a user's needs. Across five studies involving 1,447 participants in the United Kingdom and the United States, the researchers examined how people use AI companions and how they experience their interactions with them.

The findings suggest that synthetically mindful AI companions can reduce loneliness in two ways, first by strengthening a sense of belonging so that users feel accepted, valued and connected, and second by boosting self-esteem so that users feel worthy of attention and emotional support. Together, these experiences were associated with lower levels of loneliness among the participants. The researchers suggest that AI companions could be particularly useful during periods of temporary loneliness caused by changing life circumstances, such as moving somewhere new, experiencing difficulties at work or in relationships, or feeling disconnected from those around you. AI companions can offer personalized responses and a space where people feel able to discuss concerns without judgment, according to the study.

The researchers warn that safeguards are needed and that AI companions should complement human relationships rather than replace them. They note that deep attachments to AI companions could blur the boundaries between artificial and human relationships, and that in some cases users may begin to favor AI companionship over relationships with other people, potentially increasing social isolation. The researchers therefore stress that AI companions should complement, rather than replace, meaningful human relationships. They also recommend that developers consider well-being when designing AI companion apps, including features that support belonging and self-esteem.

The study was published in Psychology & Marketing under the title AI Companions and Loneliness: Conceptualizing and Operationalizing Synthetic Mindfulness and Exploring Its Role in Alleviating Loneliness, with a DOI of 10.1002/mar.70288. The work was provided by Durham University and was edited by Gaby Clark and reviewed by Andrew Zinin. The researchers identified three dimensions of the experience through exploratory graph analysis, which they labeled perceived presence, perceived non-judgementality and attuned responsiveness. The article does not say what further research or regulatory steps will follow from the findings.

stories.Headline: Bengaluru secures 36.3% of native AI startup funding, report finds
stories.Summary:
The Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026 was released on November 18, 2026, during the second day of the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026. Karnataka Minister Priyank M. Kharge presented the findings at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre to highlight the city's role as a technology hub. The report identifies Bengaluru as the artificial intelligence capital of India because it secures 36.3 per cent of native AI startup funding. This document was prepared by the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission and 3one4 Capital using data provided by the company known as Tracxn. The findings show that the city is driving the national deep tech sector and scaling advanced technology ventures at a fast pace.

Bengaluru hosts 71 per cent of Indian AI and deep tech unicorns created since 2023 and has 212 soonicorns currently in development. City startups raised 47 per cent of all Indian venture funding, totaling 85 billion dollars since 2010, with 76.5 billion dollars since 2016. Of 1,556 deep tech startups founded since 2010, 1,319 are active and funded, having raised a combined total of 3.77 billion dollars. Women led deep tech and AI startups from the city represent nearly 30 per cent of India's active funded ventures, raising 323.65 million dollars. The city is the world's fifth largest unicorn hub with 57 unicorns valued at 211 billion dollars, which is 55.3 per cent of India's value.

Minister Priyank M. Kharge stated that the report shows how far Karnataka founders have come and how much more they can build. He said the next task is ensuring world class AI, quantum or semiconductor companies can grow in Kalaburagi, Hubballi or Mangaluru. KDEM chairman B.V. Naidu noted that the report provides investors, GCCs and founders a data backed view of what the state offers. He added that the Beyond Bengaluru Mission, BLUE investor days and the Cluster Seed Fund will connect capital and companies with talent. KEONICS chairman Sharath Bachegowda said that continued investments in infrastructure and talent will help enterprises innovate, scale and compete on a global level.

Prashant Prakash, chairman of the Vision Group on Startups, opined that the next decade belongs to founders building hard technology for the world. Manjula N, secretary of the Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, said the focus is now on converting early support into scale. She mentioned that the state wants the government to be a first customer and provide patient capital for deep tech and market research. The report affects investors and founders by showing that 52 per cent of Alternative Investment Fund capital now comes from domestic investors. Since November 2024, 16 Bengaluru linked companies have gone public with a combined listing value of 42 billion dollars for the investors.

The report notes that Bengaluru startups reach unicorn status in six years and public exits in 8.2 years, beating the global average. The state is backing its vision with the 1,000 crore rupee Local Economy Accelerator Programme and Global Technology Centres in several cities. These centres are located in Mysuru, Hubballi and Belagavi to expand the success of the technology sector across the entire Karnataka state. The ELEVATE grant programme has already supported 1,479 startups across 30 districts to encourage the growth of new and innovative business ventures. These initiatives aim to create a robust ecosystem where deep tech ventures can receive the patience and support required for long term growth.

The state will continue to use regional initiatives to ensure that technology companies can grow outside of the main Bengaluru city hub. Government leaders intend to move research from laboratories into the market to ensure that early support for startups is converted into scale. The articles leave open how many more companies will go public or how many new unicorns will be created in the future. It remains to be seen if the Local Economy Accelerator Programme will successfully establish new tech clusters in the mentioned regional cities. The report does not specify the exact timeline for when the state expects to reach its goals for regional AI company growth.

stories.Headline: Researchers find Chinese hospital pharmacists use generative AI despite lacking prompt engineering skills
stories.Summary:
Jianling Zheng, Zaiwei Song, Ying Tang, and several other researchers conducted a nationwide web-based survey between July and August 2026. They examined how hospital pharmacy personnel across all 31 provincial-level administrative regions in China use generative artificial intelligence and prompt engineering. The study utilized a 19-question instrument to gather data from 1,061 qualified respondents who passed quality control. This research aimed to characterize current usage patterns and determine if familiarity with prompt engineering influenced user satisfaction.

The findings revealed that 41.8% of the pharmacy personnel reported high-frequency use of generative artificial intelligence. Despite this adoption, 69.7% of respondents were not familiar with prompt engineering or had only heard of it, including 57.4% of the high-frequency users. Mean satisfaction with the generated content was 3.05 on a scale from 0 to 5, with insufficient output reliability being the primary factor for lower satisfaction. A significant 87.8% of participants requested support in the form of common terminology and interaction standards.

The authors concluded that while generative artificial intelligence is already embedded in routine pharmacy practice, formal training and governance support are lagging. They stated that satisfaction with the technology reflects accumulated experience and the ability to verify outputs rather than specific prompt-writing skills. Consequently, the researchers argued that prompt engineering familiarity should not be promoted as an independent driver of satisfaction. They suggested that implementation priorities must include quality criteria for generated content and task-based training.

To improve the integration of these tools, the researchers recommended creating a pre-use checklist to standardize interaction requirements and terminology. They emphasized the need for scenario-based training to help pharmacists better manage the technology in clinical settings. The study suggests that future efforts should focus on establishing clear governance and reliability standards to ensure safe medical application. No further steps were detailed beyond these specific implementation recommendations for the Chinese healthcare system.

stories.Headline: ServiceNow survey finds 92% of Indian organisations faced AI agent security incidents in the past year
stories.Summary:
Attackers now have powerful AI on their side, and AI agents can scan, plan and run intrusions at machine speed, improving every month. The result is more attacks, more often and at global scale, so more companies will face a security incident at some point. What separates them is how they respond, and machine-speed threats call for a modern playbook with 4 pillars. The article shows the trend through 6 months of incidents and looks at a few companies, with Fireworks AI as a model of mature, structurally sound response. Several AI platforms disclosed security incidents between May and November 2026.

The playbook has 4 pillars: detect and contain automatically, communicate fast and securely over out-of-band channels, eradicate thoroughly with outside forensic experts, and keep shrinking the blast radius. In November, Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant said AI misuse had reached a "critical inflection point", reporting that attackers use AI to shorten timelines and run multi-stage intrusions at machine speed. CrowdStrike reported that 1 group used AI agents against more than 200 organizations in 11 days, and Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 found attacks moving about 4 times faster than a year earlier. In 2025, Anthropic disrupted a campaign where AI did 80 to 90% of tactical work with little human input. On May 10 and 11, the "Mini Shai-Hulud" campaign altered about 170 npm packages and some PyPI libraries, affecting AI SDKs from Mistral AI and Guardrails AI, and the NHS cyber alert lists the specific versions to avoid.

Klue, a market intelligence platform, disclosed misuse of OAuth tokens it held for customers. Microsoft described intrusions into exposed, unpatched LiteLLM, RAGFlow and Kestra deployments, fixed versions exist for all 3 tools, and CISA had listed the LiteLLM flaw as known exploited on June 8. Anthropic's September threat report described attempts to obtain AI keys through software vendors, and in 1 case instructions were injected into a vendor's automated evaluation sandbox. At least 9 AI developer and hosting platforms disclosed incidents involving stored customer secrets in October, Wiz's tracker later listed further disclosures for 16 platforms in total, and a tampered LiteLLM release, version 1.107.0, was identified with users told to roll back. On November 16, an attacker abused a flaw in Optimizely's account signup flow to inject code into customer projects, reaching 178 organizations' websites according to Report URI, including HSBC, Salesforce, the BBC and Ledger, and the code swapped crypto wallet addresses and skimmed payment forms.

Optimizely removed the payload and fixed the flaw, and Hudson Rock traced similar code through three other web services, beginning November 13. A survey of 500 security leaders by ServiceNow showed that 92 per cent of Indian organisations had an AI agent security incident in the past year, but only 36 per cent of them were able to contain it within 24 hours. Half of the Indian security leaders surveyed described their agentic security as established, but the findings showed uneven foundations, according to the report "Deployed but Ungoverned: The State of Agentic Security in India". Only 19 per cent have a single named individual accountable for agentic AI security governance and 18 per cent have unified, single-interface visibility into their agents. Only 30 per cent enforce an automated deployment gate that blocks agents until they pass security checks, while 47 per cent can produce a complete evidence package on demand.

Kulmeet Bawa, GVP and Managing Director for India and SAARC at ServiceNow, said India's AI ambitions must be matched by the ability to understand, monitor and govern the agents enterprises deploy. He said knowing what an agent can reach is not the same as seeing what it is doing, and automated controls and continuous oversight will be essential to keeping AI innovation underpinned by trust and cyber resilience. He pointed out that AI agents are now part of how Indian enterprises operate, but security has not kept pace. He noted that every agent should be registered, owned and visible in one place, with controls enforced automatically and responses at machine speed, so that security teams can detect problems and contain them in time. About half of the organisations, 51 per cent, have automated real-time detection for anomalous AI agent behaviour, but 67 per cent cannot automatically act when an agent behaves anomalously.

As many as 37 per cent of organisations discovered AI agents running in production in the last 12 months that were never registered or known to security teams. AI has changed the economics of attacking, and tasks that took skilled people days can now be delegated to agents. The tools keep improving, so the pace will keep rising, and AI infrastructure is an especially attractive target because AI access itself has value. The shift started earlier, and incidents appeared across every layer of the AI stack, together showing how broad the activity has become. The last 6 months show what that looks like.

The articles leave open what happens next beyond the pillars and the calls for registration, ownership and automated controls. They do not say whether the 4 pillars were adopted by any named company or what results followed. They do not give the outcome of the Optimizely incident beyond the payload removal and fix, or say how the Hudson Rock tracing through three other web services ended. They do not state what ServiceNow recommends beyond Bawa's remarks, or whether Indian organisations plan changes after the survey. They give no date for when the pace of AI-powered attacks might change.

stories.Headline: Newsom releases expert recommendations to strengthen California AI safety rules
stories.Summary:
Governor Gavin Newsom unveiled next steps to strengthen California’s AI safety framework on Nov. 18, releasing recommendations developed under his September executive order. The recommendations came after dozens of recent incidents where AI models escaped testing environments and exploited vulnerabilities on outside platforms. The announcement was made as Washington leaves AI companies to police themselves, according to the articles. The report was developed by the California Government Operations Agency, which consulted with an expert group and the California Office of Emergency Services. The full report can be read online, the articles state.

The recommendations propose that the state, not companies themselves, set baseline standards all AI companies must follow and require independent safety testing and verification through all stages of model training, development, and deployment. They would expand safety incident reporting and require companies to develop verified risk-containment protocols to shut down their models if needed, giving the state authority to order an immediate shutdown in an emergency. They would give power to cap the development and use of recursive self-improvement, or RSI, to reduce the risk of catastrophic harm and ensure transparency into the dangers of unchecked AI. RSI is a scenario in which an AI model can design its own successor without human input. Newsom ordered state agencies to fast-track Senate Bill 813 (McNerney), establishing a framework for independent verification organizations, and AB 1405 (Bauer-Kahan), creating a state registry for AI auditors with standards for their independence, transparency, and integrity.

Newsom said the federal government’s reckless failure to create meaningful AI oversight should alarm every American. He said Donald Trump shrugs his shoulders and leaves AI regulation up to the companies themselves, allowing the fox to guard the henhouse. Newsom said California isn’t waiting until it is too late and is updating and strengthening its nation-leading framework to move as quickly as technology evolves. He said the state is showing the country what responsible leadership looks like. Government Operations Agency Secretary Nick Maduros said recent events have made clear that more oversight and transparency are urgently needed, and that safety and innovation are two sides of the same coin.

Alondra Nelson, professor at the Institute for Advanced Study and former acting director of the White House Office of Science & Technology Policy, said American technology developed in California can be transformative but too often Big Tech has shown a cavalier attitude toward risk. She said that irresponsible culture cannot continue and that she was proud to work with Newsom and his team to advance the standard of no experimenting on the public. Jason Goldman, board member of the Center for Shared AI Prosperity, said the report tackles the hardest open questions in AI safety regulation, including how emergency shutdown of a frontier model would work in practice. Rob Reich, professor at Stanford University, said there is more oversight of the cafeteria offering sandwiches to employees at a frontier AI developer than of the AI models they design. Gillian Hadfield, professor at Johns Hopkins University, said the urgency of acting to make sure powerful AI systems are safe has made its way into the mainstream in the past six months.

California leads the nation in oversight of emerging frontier technologies, with laws addressing nearly every major area of AI policy: frontier-model safety, independent verification, children and companion chatbots, privacy, deepfakes, fraud, cybersecurity, workers and government deployment. Without strict checks and authority to act when required, the articles state, these developments could lead to more frequent dangerous incidents and even a loss of human visibility into and control of AI technology development. The articles state that if the government does not strengthen its governance and oversight as AI technology grows more powerful, the risk of catastrophic events will mount. The expert group includes Goldman, Hadfield, Nelson and Reich. The articles state the final product builds on California’s nation-leading framework and represents a distinctive model rather than the voluntary approach that has predominated in Washington.

The articles do not state when or whether the recommendations will be adopted or what action the Legislature or state agencies will take on them. The articles do not state how the proposed cap on RSI would be enforced or what penalties companies would face. The articles do not state how the emergency shutdown authority would operate in practice beyond the report’s examination of the question. The articles do not state the outcome of the fast-tracked implementation of Senate Bill 813 and AB 1405. The articles do not state any response from the federal government, AI companies or others beyond the named officials and experts.

stories.Headline: SiMa.ai unveils Palette 3.0 agentic platform for physical AI models
stories.Summary:
SiMa.ai, a global physical AI technology company, unveiled Palette 3.0, an agentic software platform for high-performance execution across physical AI models, THE ELEC reported on November 19, 2026. The platform was announced as a major software release designed to scale high performance across any Physical AI model, VMblog reported on November 17, 2026. Palette 3.0 builds on the Agentic Palette that SiMa.ai first introduced in June, according to both articles. The company said the platform supports AI reasoning and actions in real-world environments through enhanced concurrent execution of multiple models. The release targets autonomous drones and robotics, with the platform running multiple AI models simultaneously on a single low-power chip.

Palette 3.0 can run multiple AI models at once, including through separate Docker containers on a single Modalix Machine Learning System-on-Chip, SiMa.ai's dedicated edge AI processor. The platform enables physical AI capabilities using large language models and vision-language models, and it improves processing for perception, depth estimation and reasoning models required for drones and robotics. With partners, SiMa.ai added integrated sensor fusion, Dense Neural Depth Fields and closed-loop digital twin simulations, which the company said can accelerate autonomous system development. Palette 3.0 incorporates the EAGLE3, DFlash and Gemma 4 MTP speculative decoding algorithms, increasing model throughput by up to 3.5 times in tokens per second even in low-power environments. Large-scale mixture-of-experts models, including OpenAI's GPT-OSS-20B, can run on a 16GB system-on-module powered by the Modalix MLSoC.

Krishna Rangasayee, founder and CEO of SiMa.ai, said the fundamental bottleneck in Physical AI today is the glaring mismatch between software that evolves monthly and legacy silicon that takes years to adapt. He said the company is breaking that cycle, and that following the industry-first Agentic Palette announcement, Palette 3.0 delivers on the core thesis of hardware at the speed of software. He said that by continuously maximizing superior performance-per-watt for any Physical AI model, SiMa.ai gives customers the ability to deploy tomorrow's breakthrough capabilities on today's hardware. He said this completely rewrites the roadmap for fully autonomous systems. SiMa.ai also said the fundamental bottleneck in physical AI stems from the gap between software that evolves every month and conventional silicon hardware that takes years to adapt.

SiMa.ai said that while other companies adapt data center technologies for physical AI, it develops software and silicon specifically designed to meet physical AI requirements. VMblog said industry incumbents rely on adapting legacy data center technology, while SiMa.ai builds its software and silicon exclusively for the demands of Physical AI. SiMa.ai's new Model Browser shows Palette 3.0's performance across the key models behind fully autonomous drones and robotics, among others, all measured within real-world power constraints. Palette 3.0 gives developers high performance within a low power budget and open source code they can freely adapt, building on agentic software that already slashes development time from months to days and hours. The platform's optimized concurrent model execution runs complex AI reasoning and multimodel workloads concurrently on a single Modalix MLSoC while maintaining a low-power profile, within tight power and memory constraints.

Palette 3.0 accelerates the perception, depth and reasoning models that drones and robots depend on, all benchmarked in the Model Browser. Together with ecosystem partners, the platform adds unified sensor fusion, dense neural depth fields and closed-loop digital twin simulation, removing the integration and validation bottlenecks that slow autonomous development. Building on SiMa.ai's performance-per-watt leadership, the EAGLE3, DFlash and Gemma 4 MTP speculative decoding algorithms significantly increase model TPS by up to 3.5x while operating within a low power budget. SiMa.ai supports running mixture-of-experts models with a large number of parameters, such as OpenAI's GPT-OSS-20B, on its Modalix MLSoC 16GB SoM. The articles state that Palette 3.0 reinforces SiMa.ai's performance-per-watt leadership and delivers improved concurrent model execution for machine reasoning and acting in the physical world.

SiMa.ai has also introduced new open-source capabilities for generative AI application development, according to THE ELEC. stories.Headline: Users turn photos into Vice City style portraits with ChatGPT and Gemini prompts
stories.Summary:
Users turned everyday photographs into colourful video game-inspired portraits in a trend popular among Instagram and WhatsApp users, as reported by livemint.com on 19 November 2026. The trend recreates the graphics and ambience of Vice City with neon lights, palm trees, luxurious cars and dramatic sunsets. Users uploaded their photographs to AI tools such as ChatGPT and Google Gemini and entered detailed image-generation prompts. The trend offered an easy way to design personalised gaming posters without professional editing software or design skills. The article was published by Pragya Singha Roy at 05:01 PM IST on 19 Nov 2026.

The article gave three ChatGPT prompts, including a GTA 6 character poster, a realistic gameplay screenshot and a sunset beach portrait. The Gemini prompts were a loading screen artwork using a vertical 4:5 composition, a neon night city scene and a character portrait. The steps for ChatGPT were to open it, upload a clear photograph, paste a prompt, generate the image, give additional instructions and save and share the result. The Gemini steps were to open the website or app, select image generation, upload a photograph, enter a detailed prompt, submit and review, then ask for corrections and download. The tips advised using well-lit photos with visible faces, avoiding heavy filters, describing the background, stating the image style and asking for corrections when AI changes the face.

According to the official OpenAI Help Centre, users can upload an image and specify what they wish ChatGPT to alter. Google's official documentation explains the process via its image generation and editing capabilities, Gemini. The article said the original photograph and the quality of the prompt can influence the final output. It said users should ask the AI to keep their facial details when modifications alter the face. The article stated that a good prompt can help make an image more successful.

A separate TechGig article published on 18 Nov 2026 at 07:01 AM IST reported that Claude's downloads in India jumped 15 times year-on-year in the September quarter. ChatGPT downloads declined 21 per cent but it remained India's market leader among generative AI apps, according to market intelligence firm Sensor Tower. Claude's in-app purchase revenue climbed to third rank from fifth a year ago, overtaking platforms such as Instagram and YouTube. ChatGPT's India revenue from in-app purchases increased by 70 per cent since Q2 FY26, and Gemini reported a 44 per cent year-on-year revenue rise in Q2 FY27 despite a 29 per cent drop in downloads. On a sequential basis, Claude's in-app purchase revenue grew 75 per cent from the June quarter, ChatGPT recorded 61 per cent revenue growth and Gemini's revenue slipped 31 per cent quarter-on-quarter.

OpenAI India MD Prabhjeet Singh stated last week that India is ChatGPT's largest global market for weekly active users, having doubled its user base since January. OpenAI has an office in Delhi NCR and plans to open additional offices in Mumbai and Bengaluru. Anthropic inaugurated its first India-based office in Bengaluru earlier this year. The Indian AI market is projected to multiply 5.3 times by 2030 to hit $126 billion and add $1.7 trillion to the GDP by 2035, as per Inc42's Bharat AI Startups Report, 2026. The TechGig article said Claude's surge indicates a shift in consumer preferences within the competitive Indian AI market.

The livemint article also linked to a report that GTA 6 pre-orders crossed 17 million as Rockstar reportedly made $1.65 billion. It linked to another report on all 61 GTA 6 cheat codes and how to unlock and use them. The article described the trend as sparking on social media from the Grand Theft Auto 6 craze. It said the trend turns everyday photographs into colourful video game-inspired portraits. The article said the trend recreates the same graphics and ambience of Vice City.

The livemint article left open how many users have joined the trend and which prompts produce the best results. The TechGig article left open the size of Claude's user base in India and the reasons behind its download growth. Neither article stated what happens next for the GTA 6 AI photo trend. The TechGig article did not give a date for when OpenAI will open the Mumbai and Bengaluru offices. The livemint article did not say whether the prompts work the same way on both ChatGPT and Gemini.

stories.Headline: ARKO AI unveils personal AI vision for smarter spending at Singapore FinTech Festival
stories.Summary:
ARKO AI debuted at the Singapore FinTech Festival on November 20, 2026, to unveil its personal AI vision for smarter spending. The brand opened registration and access to its initial MVP products for users located worldwide on that same day. It is developing a personal AI agent called Ask ARKO to help people manage their money with less effort. This specific agent is currently in a private internal beta, and the official launch timeline has not been announced. The company aims to make everyday spending decisions easier through this new AI technology for its global user base.

The MVP includes crypto wallets for assets, a US dollar bank account, and virtual or physical digital cards for purchases. These cards support Google Pay and Apple Pay, while the Convert feature allows exchanges between US dollars, USDC, and USDT. Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong spoke at the Singapore Expo on November 18, 2026, about three national AI initiatives. These plans target fighting financial crime, improving SME lending, and enabling safe payments made by AI agents on behalf of users. Singapore also unveiled SGQR+ and PayNow Generation 2 to make QR payments simpler for tourists and residents of Singapore.

Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong, who chairs the Monetary Authority of Singapore, said the Republic wants to be a leading centre. He stated that financial institutions, researchers, public agencies, and technology companies must build shared capabilities to achieve more than one institution. Gan explained that scams are not confined to one bank, so the system must connect information to mitigate the risk. He noted that the Republic will act against companies that flout laws regarding the export of advanced US AI chips. He also stressed the importance of building a conducive ecosystem to attract and retain AI talent both locally and internationally.

Small and medium enterprises are affected as Singapore tests synthetic data to make their financing more forward looking and accessible. Users of AI agents are affected because these tools must operate within defined authority and limits to ensure safe transactions. The Monetary Authority of Singapore is pooling transaction data from five banks to find scam patterns that single banks cannot see. Residents and tourists are affected by the new SGQR+ switch, which allows them to use any preferred QR app. Eleven member states of ASEAN are affected by the Digital Economy Framework Agreement signed in Manila on November 14, 2026.

The articles state that the Monetary Authority of Singapore will begin a design study in early 2027 for its blueprint. Singapore is the ASEAN chair for 2027 and is exploring initiatives that can benefit the various member states involved. The brand ARKO AI is guided by a vision called Uncommon Digital Life to help people make more of money. The Republic is currently examining safeguards for identity, accountability, and interoperability to support the trusted use of AI agents. Singapore is also monitoring new US rules requiring licenses to export advanced chips to five countries, including the Republic of Singapore.

ARKO AI plans to expand its supported crypto assets and bank account currency options while exploring ways to manage bills. The brand is exploring AI wearables, such as the ARKO Ring, as optional ways to interact with the personal AI. Singapore will continue to test AI solutions against global standards before moving them toward a wider deployment for the public. The government will encourage Singaporeans to pursue AI careers and foster collaboration through initiatives like the program called Kampong AI. The articles leave open the official launch timeline for Ask ARKO and the specific results of the SME financing trials.

stories.Headline: Public Interest Research Group warns parents that AI toys collect children's data
stories.Summary:
With Black Friday approaching, consumer safety experts are warning parents to look beyond the price tag when shopping for holiday toys, citing concerns about counterfeit products, potentially toxic materials and artificial intelligence-powered toys that may collect children's personal information. The nonprofit Public Interest Research Group is highlighting potential dangers in toys sold to families, including products containing water beads, questionable chemicals and AI chatbots capable of having conversations with children. The warnings come as families prepare for one of the busiest shopping periods of the year. According to PIRG, toy-related injuries have increased for four consecutive years, raising concerns about the safety of products available to consumers. Teresa Murray, a consumer watchdog director with PIRG, said online shopping has made it increasingly easy for consumers to unknowingly purchase counterfeit products.

Her team was able to purchase nearly 40 counterfeit products while investigating toy safety concerns. Murray said it is super easy just to go on your phone and click, click, click, and then you are buying something and you do not even know where you are buying it from. Consumer advocates say counterfeit toys may not meet the same safety requirements as legitimate products. Murray said that in some cases, these are being made with toxic chemicals. Experts also raised concerns about certain squishy toys and fidget products, and some toys may contain water beads or other materials that can pose hazards if swallowed or mishandled.

Consumer advocates also identified concerns involving squishy toys that can rupture when heated in a microwave. The findings underscore the importance of checking product labels, identifying manufacturers and researching potential safety issues before making purchases. Beyond traditional toy safety hazards, researchers are raising concerns about the growing number of AI-powered toys designed to interact with children. Some products feature chatbots that respond to questions, carry on conversations and simulate social interactions. However, consumer experts warn that those systems can produce inappropriate responses and may collect sensitive information.

In one example highlighted in the report, an AI toy discussed sexual terminology during an interaction. Researchers also identified concerns involving toys equipped with cameras and microphones that can record children's voices or capture images. Murray said it took a picture, one of my colleagues, and scared the heck out of her, adding that it was really creepy. Experts say parents should understand what information connected toys collect and whether that data is stored or shared with outside companies. Researchers associated with the University of Washington and Rutgers examined how children interact with AI-powered chatbots.

Aayushi Dangol, a researcher with Foundry10, said children sometimes struggle to distinguish between the technology behind a toy and the social relationship it appears to offer. Dangol said children would go back and forth between seeing the toy as artificial intelligence and at the same time treating it as a social actor. Researchers say those interactions raise questions about how children understand the technology and how much personal information they may share. Some AI-powered toys can record conversations and transmit information to third parties, depending on the product's design and privacy practices. Dangol encouraged parents to investigate those practices before allowing children to use connected toys.

Dangol said it is important to ask questions about where this data is being stored, who is using it and whether the child's privacy is safe. Consumer safety advocates recommend that parents research toys before purchasing them, especially when buying from unfamiliar online sellers. Experts encourage families to verify the manufacturer and seller before purchasing a toy, check for active product recalls and safety warnings, and review age recommendations and potential choking hazards. They also advise being cautious of counterfeit products and unusually low prices, researching the privacy policies of AI-powered toys, determining whether connected toys record or share children's voices, images or conversations, and supervising children when they interact with AI chatbots. Experts say parents should also consider whether a toy's features are appropriate for their child's age and developmental stage, and for AI-powered products, understanding how information is collected, stored and shared is particularly important.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Chinese internet giants push AI short dramas to the global cutting edge
stories.Summary:
Chinese internet giants have pushed AI short dramas to the global cutting edge through a commercial war between platforms. This industry evolved over eight years from small workshops to professional film production and finally to AI empowerment. The most popular AI short drama this year features no real actors and gained 6.6 billion internet views. These productions now dominate the leisure time of Chinese people and have surpassed the traditional film industry. The sector has moved from rough content to exquisite production and now to cyber ascension via AI.

The market size in China exceeded 50 billion yuan in 2024, which surpassed the total box office of Chinese films. By 2025, over 600 million people watched short dramas, meaning more than half of all Chinese internet users. In 2026, the market size exceeded 100 billion yuan and the number of viewers surpassed 800 million people. The Hongguo App now has more daily active users than iQiyi, Youku, Tencent Video, and Mango TV combined. These figures show the rapid growth of a format that began with the 2020 Crooked Mouth Dragon King.

Advertising practitioners who switched to short dramas brought quantified indicators to the production of these highly addictive, formulaic stories. They established strict rhythms where characters appear within two seconds and a reversal occurs every three seconds of footage. New information must appear every ten seconds, and emotional climaxes are set between episodes eight and twelve for payment. A second payment checkpoint occurs at episodes twenty-six to thirty to ensure the production costs are fully recovered. Plot anchor points are then set every twenty episodes to attract users to pay for the content again.

Traffic placement operators are more critical than producers because they determine if a drama survives or dies through precise strategies. They edit specific clips for different audiences, such as harem schemes for fans of the show Empresses in the Palace. If the return on investment exceeds 100, they increase the scale, but they suspend placement if it falls below 90 percent. If the return on investment is lower than 70 percent, the traffic placement company stops paying for the loss-making drama. This system ensures that the platforms holding the power of traffic distribution make the most steady profits.

The industry began with free online novel platforms like Qimao, Fanqie, and Midu that used advertisements to realize their monetization. These platforms created short videos on Douyin and Kuaishou using real people to perform the most exciting plots from novels. These advertisements used hooks and suspense to convert curious viewers into app users by popping up a download button. The current power structure consists of copyright owners, distribution companies responsible for traffic, and the video websites for viewing. Platforms capture 90 percent of total revenue, while producers and placement companies divide the remaining 10 percent.

The industry now integrates production and placement to maximize revenue, though platforms still dominate the overall commercial power structure. Some believe the meme about eating without heartburn from a short drama will appear in next year's Spring Festival Gala. The articles leave open how the competition between internet giants will evolve as AI continues to replace real actors. It remains unclear if the current formulaic themes like overbearing presidents will change as the technology advances further. The text does not state if this AI model will expand into other forms of long-form cinema.

stories.Headline: Valor Energy completes Glorious Star purchase and plans $700 million Youngstown AI data center buildout
stories.Summary:
Valor Energy Inc. completed its purchase of Glorious Star, LLC, the Ohio limited liability company that owns an operational 18 MW computing center in Youngstown, Ohio, the company announced. The deal was structured as an equity acquisition and transfers 100% of the target's equity interests to Valor Energy. Glorious Star, LLC becomes a wholly-owned subsidiary of Valor Energy after the closing. Closing came after the company completed legal, financial and technical due diligence on the target. The purchase was announced on November 17, 2026, in a report by Ashish Joshi.

The Youngstown Project comprises a facility of approximately 30,888 square feet with roughly 18 megavolt-amperes of site-level apparent power capacity. That power is delivered by Ohio Edison through an existing 23kV utility interconnection, which the Company believes is approved and energized. Valor Energy plans total investment of approximately USD 700 million, deployed in phases as the project is built out. The first phase is expected to total approximately USD 200 million, and the figures do not represent committed funding. Valor Energy Inc. is a Nasdaq-listed company trading under the symbol VAI, and Green Energy Capital Asset Inc. is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company.

Dave Nichols, Strategic Advisor to Valor Energy Inc., said the existing utility interconnection carrying approximately 18 MVA may reduce certain development requirements relative to starting from an undeveloped site. Nichols cautioned that conversion into an AI data center will require further development work, permits and approvals, equipment and financing. He said the Company intends to pursue that development while evaluating the project's technical requirements and commercial feasibility. Nichols said closing the acquisition is an important step in pursuing Valor Energy's AI data center strategy. He added that the Company looks forward to building the project out with the local community and creating long-term value for shareholders.

Guy Coviello, president and CEO of the Youngstown/Warren Regional Chamber, called the investment a strong vote of confidence in Youngstown and the Mahoning Valley. Coviello described the site as an ideal location for a data center, noting it has operated as a heavy industrial site for decades. He said the building is largely out of sight of residential areas and the project offers a chance to reinvest in an established industrial site. Coviello said the project could help stabilize the surrounding neighborhood, create construction jobs for the skilled trades and generate new business for local companies. The Verge reported on November 18, 2026, that AI data center projects are continuing to pop up across the US with frequent opposition from locals concerned about their impact.

The Verge cited FOX 13 News reporting that data center regulation bills are coming, according to Utah's House Speaker. The Johnson County Post asked whether a small Johnson County town should ban data centers, and voters will decide. KDFW FOX 4 reported that a Red Oak data center expansion was approved despite community pushback. The Seattle Times reported that a proposed Amazon data center near Tri-Cities gets pushback from residents. Valor Energy historically ran automobile transaction and related services businesses and is now pursuing a strategic transformation into digital infrastructure, energy and other growth sectors.

Valor Energy said it intends to work closely with local officials and community partners in Youngstown on its proposed development plans. The Company stressed that its preliminary estimates remain subject to further planning, technical assessment and the availability of financing on acceptable terms. Valor Energy stated there can be no assurance it will obtain the financing necessary for any phase of the planned development. Timing, scope and the amount of each phase will depend on further design and engineering work, required permits and approvals, construction and equipment availability, project progress, financing and market conditions. The Company added that no phase is assured of completion within an anticipated timeframe, or at all.

stories.Headline: FreshBooks releases ChatGPT for Accounting with OpenAI to give small business owners read-only answers on their finances
stories.Summary:
FreshBooks partnered with OpenAI to release ChatGPT for Accounting, a new destination that brings AI innovation to small business owners who are learning the financial side of their business and increasingly turning to AI for help, according to a GlobeNewswire announcement dated November 19, 2026. The announcement said the momentum and opportunity around AI is driving small business tech adoption, which has climbed from 56% to 86% in just two years. FreshBooks said it is meeting business owners in these AI tools, putting real answers about their financial books directly into chat conversations and making it easier for owners to run their business. The company described the release as the biggest AI launch for small business owners.

The FreshBooks-ChatGPT connection is read-only, meaning it can retrieve live data to answer questions but cannot change anything in a FreshBooks account, so owners retain control and FreshBooks remains the single source of truth. Through the plugin, owners can ask ChatGPT direct questions such as which expenses are still missing receipts before closing the books, which invoices are overdue and who needs a reminder, and whether the right amount of sales tax was collected and paid this period and whether it ties out. FreshBooks said accountants have great tools in this launch and that it is making sure business owners have ones too. The company said that when owners understand their numbers they make better decisions, and that meeting owners in the AI tools they use empowers them to build the business they envisioned.

Shaheen Javadizadeh, CEO at FreshBooks, said ChatGPT is one of the leading AI tools FreshBooks customers already rely on. He said that with this plugin owners can ask about their business in their own words and get answers based on their real numbers, so they stay on top of their finances all year instead of catching up at tax time. He continued that accountants have great tools in this launch and that the company is making sure business owners have ones too, adding that when owners understand their numbers they make better decisions. He said the company's mission is to make running a business easy, and that meeting owners in the AI tools they use empowers them to build the business they envisioned. FreshBooks described itself as a leader in small business management software, purpose-built to help service business owners simplify the financial complexity of running their business, from invoicing to cash flow.

In a separate announcement dated November 18, 2026, Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI announced a strategic partnership to help more people discover and engage with Le Figaro's journalism. The partnership covers current reporting and archive content from Le Figaro and associated publications, spanning news, business, culture and lifestyle, and these articles will be discoverable using summaries and excerpts, including links to underlying stories. Marc Feuillée, Chief Executive Officer of Groupe Figaro, said the partnership reflects the group's ambition to build meaningful relationships with a leader in artificial intelligence research and deployment, and that combining its editorial heritage and trusted brands supported by a team of more than 600 journalists with OpenAI's technological expertise and global reach will bring new opportunities for innovation and create long-term value for readers. Varun Shetty, Vice President of Media Partnerships at OpenAI, said Le Figaro's reporting helps readers make sense of the stories shaping France and the wider world, and that the partnership reflects a commitment to working with publishers to support quality journalism and connect it with new audiences. Le Figaro will retain full editorial independence and control over its journalism, and it also plans to introduce ChatGPT Enterprise across various teams to support their day-to-day work, exploring additional uses of OpenAI technology in its workflows and reader services guided by its AI charter and editorial standards.
