stories.Headline: MFour adds Google AI Mode to its consumer conversation feed and collects 2.8 million new AI conversations every 30 days
stories.Summary:
MFour Data Research, Inc., a provider of the largest mobile-app consumer panel in the U.S., announced on November 20, 2026, that it has added Google AI Mode to its AI conversation data feed. The Irvine, California, company said the addition means it now collects 2.8 million new consumer AI conversations every 30 days. Google AI Mode joins ChatGPT and Google Gemini in the feed, which MFour describes as the only platform connecting surveys and behaviors for full journey intelligence from prompt to purchase. The announcement builds on MFour's November 3 announcement that it had added Google Gemini, which expanded its collection from 2.35 million to 2.8 million new AI conversations every 30 days.

The addition gives clients greater scale and a broader view of how consumers use AI to research products and make decisions, according to the release. Google AI Mode lets consumers research products, compare brands and refine their choices through conversations within Google Search, and MFour connects those exchanges to the same consumers' subsequent behaviors. Brands and agencies can ask DANI, MFour's autonomous AI research analyst, to analyze AI conversations alongside connected behavioral and survey data and produce boardroom-ready reports. The AI conversation feed is also available for direct licensing, and MFour says the signals reveal what consumers are considering, what they do next and why.

Chris St. Hilaire, CEO of MFour Data Research, said a company cannot claim to understand its consumer if it is blind to the conversations shaping their decisions. He said customers are asking AI what to buy and which brands to trust, and that MFour connects those conversations to what they actually do next. He said this gives insights teams the power to walk into the boardroom with answers the business can act on, including what consumers want, what is winning their consideration and where to go next. MFour connects conversation data to the same consumer's demographics, web browsing, app usage, GPS-verified store visits, purchases and survey responses through a single identity.

MFour, founded in 2011, says its 14M+ consumer panel generates nine deterministic data streams all connected to a single identity, and that DANI provides analysis across 4 billion monthly buyer signals. The data comes from MFour's first-party panel, whose members opt in and are compensated for sharing their behavioral data and participating in surveys. The company says it is trusted by Samsung, Google, Amazon Ads, Microsoft, Hulu, Keurig Dr Pepper, Papa Johns and hundreds of other global brands. The release offers one free LLM insights report through MFour's website by providing DANI simple guidance on the insights being sought.

stories.Headline: Study Pocket launches AI simultaneous interpretation for schools in April 2027
stories.Summary:
Study Pocket Co., Ltd., a Tokyo-based company led by CEO Ryo Yamaji and CAIO Hiroyuki Tsuruta, announced on November 20, 2026 that it will officially offer its school-oriented web service "Study Pocket AI Simultaneous Interpretation" from April 2027, a tool that interprets conversations between teachers and children and students who need Japanese language instruction as well as parents with foreign roots. The service was first announced in May 2026 as "Study Pocket AI Interpreter" and was provided free of charge during the current fiscal year to teacher accounts of "Study Pocket for TEACHER," after which trial use continued at schools and municipalities that made inquiries. With the official launch the name changes to "Study Pocket AI Simultaneous Interpretation," and the pricing and timing that were undecided at the time of the announcement have now been set. The service runs in the browser of GIGA school devices without any dedicated equipment, and it supports bidirectional interpretation that displays the teacher's Japanese in the other person's language and the child's or parent's words in Japanese on the screen in real time.

The pricing is 50,000 yen per school per year, excluding tax, which covers all faculty and staff and up to five children needing Japanese instruction, with an additional 10,000 yen per year excluding tax for each person from the sixth child, and contracts are made per school and per fiscal year from April to the following March, with quotations and invoices available. The service supports 60 languages including Japanese, with Portuguese, Chinese, Filipino, English, Spanish, Vietnamese and Korean placed under frequently used languages, and it offers a face-to-face mode, full-screen display, adjustable text size, color coding by speaker, conversation records that can be reviewed later, AI summaries after a conversation and export in TXT or CSV formats. Speech recognition and interpretation use the Japan region of the voice AI Soniox, with audio sent directly from the device browser to Soniox, and schools decide the scope of use, as administrators assign children one by one from a roster. According to a May 2026 Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology survey, 84,759 children in public schools needed Japanese language instruction as of May 1, 2025, up 15,636, or 22.6 percent, from the previous survey, of whom 73,313 held foreign nationality and 11,446 held Japanese nationality, and 12,668 public schools, or 39.4 percent of all public schools, had at least one such child, while about 8,300 schools, roughly two thirds, had only one to four.

The company says it developed the service because such children are enrolled in small numbers across many schools and the languages used differ from school to school, making it difficult to station interpreters or native-language supporters at every school, so teachers often combine gestures and translation tools in class and meetings. A teacher at a public junior high school in the Chugoku and Shikoku area who used it during a three-way meeting with a parent from Vietnam said the parent tearfully told the teacher in her native language that she was truly grateful, and the teacher felt that feelings had gotten through beyond the language barrier. The company plans to hold a demonstration at its "StudyPocket Product Day 2026" online event on December 1, 2026 from 15:00 to 16:30, free with advance registration, showing the actual screen and plans for provision in fiscal 2027. Free trial use under this year's demonstration ends at the end of February 2027, and official provision begins in April 2027, with trial and demo requests handled individually.

stories.Headline: ABC Corporation uses OpenAI's dots to manage a vinyl greenhouse in a two week trial
stories.Summary:
ABC Corporation, a company based in Nagoya's Nakamura ward, said its research and development division ran an experiment from November 1 to November 15, 2026, in which OpenAI's general-purpose AI agent "dots" served as the core system for managing a vinyl greenhouse used in protected cultivation. The company reported that the trial achieved stable management of the greenhouse. The work drew on procedures the company had built up while operating its own systems. The experiment covered sensing conditions inside the house, managing water, ventilation, liquid fertilizer and nutrient solution, and adjusting lighting according to the crop's growth stage.

The trial addressed six management items, namely temperature and humidity control, water management, rolling up the greenhouse vinyl for ventilation, continuous environmental monitoring, light source management that adjusts the timing and duration of illumination to match growth stages, and liquid fertilizer and nutrient solution management. In the experiment, an IoT box gathering several sensors inside the house was made available to dots, and cameras installed in the greenhouse acted as the agent's eyes. dots grasped conditions from the camera images as well as the sensor readings and made the judgments needed for facility management. The company confirmed that this setup could carry out its existing management procedures. Previously the company had implemented in-house the software framework, or harness, that combined the functions needed for daily management.

The company said that when AI is used in agriculture, one approach is to develop custom programs for each facility and use case, but it sees a problem in that priority tends to go to implementing the functions needed on site, leaving security questions, such as what information to give the AI and which equipment operations to entrust to it, pushed back. For this project it therefore concentrated the core of facility management in dots. When expanding to other greenhouses, it aims to set common rules for the information the AI handles and the scope of operations it performs, so that measures do not vary from facility to facility and a certain security level is secured. It also aims to turn the management methods cultivated in its own house into a form that can be applied to other vinyl greenhouses, and it will study management mechanisms usable according to each facility's equipment and operations.

ABC Corporation is located at 12-8 Tsubakicho, Nakamura ward, Nagoya, in Aichi prefecture, and its representative is Kina Oda. The company was founded in February 2021, has capital of 15 million yen, is unlisted, and lists information and communication as its industry. The experiment ran for about two weeks in early November 2026. The company said it will use the knowledge gained from the experiment to research management systems that can be adapted to the equipment and operation of individual facilities.

Articles.Title: ABC Corporation succeeds in experiment to manage greenhouse cultivation using OpenAI's "dots"

stories.Headline: TeraWulf begins erecting structural steel at its 480 MW Kentucky AI campus for Anthropic
stories.Summary:
TeraWulf has moved from foundational work to vertical construction at its Justified Data Campus in Hawesville, Kentucky, where the company announced on LinkedIn that the first structural steel is going up at the Hancock County site, according to US Data Center Projects. The 480 MW facility is being purpose-built for the artificial intelligence company Anthropic, and the majority of structural steel for the first building, known as CB-1, has already been delivered and staged, with substantial deliveries also completed for CB-2. TeraWulf described the development as an important transition as it advances large-scale infrastructure built specifically for its customer Anthropic. Engineering, procurement and construction work at the site is being handled by Fluor Corporation, a partnership that has grown beyond the two companies' earlier collaborations.

The Justified Data Campus occupies a 790-acre site in Hancock County that was previously used for aluminum processing, and Century Aluminum operated at the location from 1969 until 2022, when TeraWulf acquired the property with plans to convert the long-standing industrial site into digital infrastructure. The project was announced in February, and the first facility at the campus is due to come online in 2027. Anthropic will lease capacity at the site, with Google acting as a backstop for the arrangement, and the campus is designed to support large-scale AI and high-performance computing workloads. At 480 MW of capacity, the Hawesville campus represents one of TeraWulf's largest commitments to date.

Leo Kaid, president of Fluor's advanced technologies and life sciences business line, said earlier this month that Fluor is proud to expand its partnership with TeraWulf and support the delivery of infrastructure needed to meet rapidly growing demand for artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. He added that the company's integrated engineering, procurement and construction capabilities, combined with its data center expertise and skilled workforce, position it to deliver the project with a strong focus on safety, quality and schedule certainty.

The Hawesville development is one of several projects in TeraWulf's expanding portfolio, and the company currently operates a campus outside Buffalo, New York, located at a former coal power plant where it initially mined cryptocurrency at the 180-acre site before beginning to pivot the campus toward AI and HPC uses. Core42 and Fluidstack are live customers at the New York location, and in addition to its operating site and the Hawesville campus, TeraWulf is developing sites in Maryland and Kentucky and is planning a second development in Lansing, New York. The move away from cryptocurrency mining toward AI and HPC infrastructure reflects a broader strategic direction for the company. With the majority of structural steel for CB-1 staged and substantial deliveries for CB-2 complete, the project is positioned for continued above-ground construction activity in the coming months, and the first facility is expected to come online in 2027.

Articles.Title: TeraWulf Erects Structural Steel at Kentucky AI Campus

stories.Headline: Adam Spatacco names Alphabet as the best long term AI investment among three trillion dollar companies
stories.Summary:
Adam Spatacco wrote an analysis on November 20, 2026, regarding three trillion-dollar artificial intelligence stocks. He evaluated Nvidia, Alphabet, and Anthropic to determine the best investment to hold through 2030. Anthropic completed the largest initial public offering in history on November 19, 2026. Nvidia is currently seeking a replacement for its founder, Jensen Huang. Spatacco concluded that Alphabet is the most compelling choice for long-term investors.

Anthropic has a market cap of 1.27 trillion dollars and an annualized revenue run rate of 81 billion dollars. The company has 900.9 billion dollars in infrastructure requirements, including 121.3 billion to Google by July 2033. It also owes at least 110 billion dollars to Amazon and 47.2 billion to Microsoft by June 2033. Nvidia has a market cap of 3.52 trillion dollars and reported third quarter revenue of 115.8 billion dollars. Alphabet has a market cap of 3.33 trillion dollars and reported third quarter revenue of 127.6 billion dollars.

Adam Spatacco stated that Alphabet combines a compelling business model with durable competitive advantages. He noted that Nvidia faces disorienting levels of uncertainty because of its leadership transition. Spatacco argued that Anthropic must justify an enormous valuation while financing hundreds of billions in infrastructure. He believes Alphabet is the strongest choice due to its innovation and financial resilience. He mentioned that Nvidia and Anthropic could still deliver outsize returns for some investors.

Hyperscalers like Amazon and Alphabet are developing custom AI accelerators to reduce their dependence on Nvidia GPUs. Competition from OpenAI, open-source models, and Google Gemini could pressure the pricing and profitability of Anthropic. Investors in Anthropic are paying a premium for financial results that have not yet materialized. Nvidia shareholders face risks because Jensen Huang resigned amid allegations involving ties to Chinese intelligence. These market shifts affect the risk profiles of all three trillion-dollar companies.

Nvidia saw third quarter adjusted earnings per share climb 111 percent to 2.68 dollars. Alphabet generated 26.2 billion dollars in net income with a companywide operating margin of 32 percent. Google Cloud grew 103 percent year over year to reach 30.7 billion dollars in quarterly revenue. Alphabet uses custom Tensor Processing Units to optimize costs and offer alternatives to Nvidia infrastructure. Nvidia management projected that fourth quarter revenue would land around 130 billion dollars.

Nvidia must now determine if it can maintain a culture of innovation under new leadership. Anthropic needs to prove that its accelerating revenue growth can translate into sustainable profitability. Alphabet continues to integrate Gemini models into Search, smartphones, and enterprise software to create revenue. The articles leave open whether Nvidia can overcome its leadership obstacles and maintain its technological edge. It remains unclear if Anthropic can meet its massive minimum payment commitments if customer demand falls.

stories.Headline: Chipmaker shares plunge as investors sell off artificial intelligence stocks
stories.Summary:
Shares of Micron Technology, SanDisk, and various other chipmakers plunged during early trading on Friday, November 20, 2026. This sudden decline occurred as investors remained under pressure due to a continuing selloff in technology and artificial intelligence stocks. The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell by more than 2 percent, while the S&P 500 index dropped around 1 percent. In contrast, the Dow Jones Industrial Average traded slightly higher because of gains in retail and healthcare stocks.

The market requires AI model and application revenues to reach at least $1.5 trillion by 2030 for an adequate return. UBS expects the Federal Reserve to implement 25-basis-point rate hikes in December 2026 and March 2027. Total United States technology investment in AI infrastructure could approach $5 trillion by the end of 2028. The iShares Semiconductor ETF, VanEck Semiconductor ETF, and Roundhill Memory ETF all declined by as much as 7 percent.

UBS stated that the risk-reward in equities has become more balanced following persistent pressure on cloud companies and chipmakers. The firm noted that monetary policy uncertainty added to fragile sentiment, though the structural AI investment story remains intact. An AMD spokesperson told Bloomberg that the company maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance with all applicable United States export control laws. UBS believes that the cumulative effects of higher rates will likely weigh on consumer demand.

The firm expects economic growth to remain close to the trend in 2027 with rising corporate profits. UBS predicts approximately 15 percent S&P 500 earnings growth in 2027 and sees further upside for equities. They favor financially strong hyperscalers with visible monetization and select leaders in semiconductor equipment and infrastructure software. The firm remains cautious regarding lower-quality suppliers and companies with valuations based on distant cash flows.

stories.Headline: Cranstoun sells three speculative AI holdings and buys a profitable networking business
stories.Summary:
Cranstoun, an investment management company, released its October 2026 Investor Letter, which highlighted how rising interest rates and financing pressures are reshaping opportunities in AI infrastructure. On September 16, the Federal Reserve raised rates by 0.25 percentage points to 3.75%, 4%, its first increase since July 2023. Brent crude rose from approximately $88 per barrel at the start of September to $104 mid-month before closing at $97.46. The S&P 500 slipped 0.7% in September to 7,651.54 but remained up 4.3% for the quarter. Cranstoun highlighted persistent infrastructure bottlenecks, including transformer lead times of three to five years, memory prices facing increases of up to 20%, and projected global data-center power demand of 132 gigawatts in 2026, up 27%.

Surging AI infrastructure spending reached $214B last quarter and $657B over the past year, raising financing concerns. In September, the firm sold three speculative holdings dependent on distant future profits and bought a profitable networking business, while retaining its core AI infrastructure positions. Meta Platforms is the social media and technology giant behind Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Threads, generating the vast majority of its revenue from advertising while investing heavily in AI and virtual/augmented reality through its Reality Labs division. The one-month return of Meta Platforms was -11.43% while its shares traded between $520.26 and $779.82 over the last 52 weeks. On November 19th, 2026, Meta Platforms stock closed at approximately $596.22 per share, with a market capitalization of about $1.546 trillion.

Cranstoun's October investor letter stated that Meta Platforms and 3 others account for $543 billion of that and fund it from the cash their businesses already generate. Cranstoun owns two of the four. The firm sees opportunities in persistent supply shortages but is monitoring higher energy costs, financing pressures, and the risk of reduced AI spending. While the letter acknowledged the potential of Meta Platforms as an investment, it pointed readers to billionaire-backed stocks before making their next move. Insider Monkey released an exclusive look into the hidden portfolios of the world's top fund managers. The report was titled "7 Stocks Warren Buffett & Billionaires Are Quietly Hoarding," and Insider Monkey cited 2.5 million monthly readers leveraging elite hedge fund data.

Another article covered Meta Platforms and shared Baron Capital's views on the company. Readers were directed to the hedge fund investor letters Q3 2026 page for more letters from hedge funds and other leading investors. The article was originally published at Insider Monkey. Meta Platforms, Inc. may need hundreds of billions for AI, according to a related Insider Monkey article from 9 days earlier. A Motley Fool article from 3 months earlier said Mark Zuckerberg is betting up to $145 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026. Meta stock surged 6.6% as AI spending fears suddenly eased, according to a GuruFocus.com article from 3 months earlier.

Rowan Street Capital said Meta Platforms' fundamentals outpace its stock rally, according to an Insider Monkey article from 3 months earlier. Meta Platforms rallied as AI monetization gained momentum, according to an Insider Monkey article from 24 days earlier. Meta Platforms grew revenue 28% as AI usage surged, according to an Insider Monkey article from 10 days earlier. Meta Platforms' AI agent opens a new growth opportunity, according to an Insider Monkey article from 24 days earlier. stories.Headline: Bain reports a third of US and European shoppers use AI assistants for shopping
stories.Summary:
About a third of consumers in the US and Europe use AI assistants for shopping, Bain & Company reported on November 20, 2026. Bain said AI is becoming the new search and is reshaping the top of the shopping funnel. ChatGPT alone serves 1.2 billion weekly users, Bain said. An estimated 15% to 20% of their prompts are shopping-related, up from 9% in 2025. Bain said shoppers now start with AI, which picks the best fit, not the biggest retailer.

A Bain Consumer Lab global survey found 33% of consumers in the US and 36% in Europe use AI assistants for some part of the shopping journey as of November 2026. That is up from 19% in the US and 8% in Europe in September 2025. AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude currently account for less than 1% of retailers' directly linked web traffic, according to Bain's analysis of estimates from Similarweb. Bain said AI referral traffic, though small, converts 90% better than non-AI traffic. Bain analyzed more than 4,400 shopping prompts across four retail verticals, testing more than 300,000 unique runs across the most used large language models, powered by Profound data.

Bain said retailers absent from AI responses will cede visibility, awareness, traffic, and profits. Bain said making the list requires a clear value proposition, an adaptable generative engine optimization strategy, and a focus on winning the shopper's occasion. Bain said leading retailers will build their assistants on proprietary data, using personalization, brand trust, and category expertise. Bain said a superior, well-communicated core value proposition should still win the purchase. Bain said retailers should ask whether they are winning for the things they want to be known for.

Bain said Kroger appears more often for prompts about promotion and loyalty, whereas Whole Foods outperforms on dietary needs and product selection. In Bain's grocery analysis, the top 10 sources accounted for roughly 30% of all citations across ChatGPT, Claude, and Google AI and Gemini. Bain said only 27 of the top 100 US retailers have a first-party AI assistant. A Bain survey found consumers still trust retailers' first-party assistants nearly twice as much as third-party ones. Walmart says Sparky users have up to 40% higher average order value, and Amazon says Alexa for Shopping users have about 40% higher average order value.

For Brazilian retailer Magazine Luiza, shoppers using its Lu assistant via WhatsApp convert at three times the rate of its traditional app users, Bain said. Bain said Lu earns an 85-point Net Promoter Score and 75% of payments happen on WhatsApp. Best Buy's Ask Blue launched in time for the holidays, Bain said. Carrefour's Hopla helps shoppers eat healthier with product swaps based on dietary preferences and analysis of cart and meal photos. Bain said a recent ChatGPT update sharply cut social media citations in favor of retailer websites and earned media.

Bain said more than 10 million people in the US and Canada set up agents in the six weeks after Meta's Muse launched. Shopping is the No. 1 use case, with purchases averaging more than $200, Bain said. Bain said consumer adoption is set to skyrocket in 2027 if early trends hold. Bain recommended retailers run a prompt audit before Black Friday and the final holiday rush. Bain said a solid GEO strategy never stops testing, learning, and adapting.

stories.Headline: Chinese spies use autonomous AI agents to exploit zero-day flaw and seize university server
stories.Summary:
Suspected Chinese spies used autonomous AI agents to discover and exploit a zero-day vulnerability to seize control of a university server. This campaign began on September 8 and lasted for 48 hours, targeting university networks located in East Asia outside of Mainland China. The attackers utilized an open source penetration-testing framework called Cairn to conduct multi-stage intrusions without any human assistance. These agents spent nearly a full day adapting their tactics, including failed attempts to breach a Redis server and a GPU server.

The successful attack targeted MONAI Label, which is an open-source medical imaging AI application, by exploiting a path traversal vulnerability. The AI agents mapped API endpoints and found a vulnerable upload parameter, allowing them to write files and execute a Python reverse shell as root within 11 minutes. Amazon notified the maintainers of the project, who subsequently released a security advisory and a fix for the flaw. After the initial breach, a human operator provided a proxy that allowed the agents to tunnel into a second university network running the same vulnerable code.

Amazon CISO CJ Moses reported that the Threat Intelligence Team discovered the operation on September 10 via a publicly hosted instance of Cairn. Moses stated that the agents demonstrated an ability to adapt for nearly a full day without human direction, showing that autonomous frameworks are now used for espionage. He noted that the prompts were written in Simplified Chinese and the scripts used China Standard Time. This discovery aligns with a report from Gambit Security documenting a Chinese operator using Cairn to compromise at least 27 companies during September.

The broader context reveals that these AI harnesses are being adopted for both criminal operations and state-sponsored espionage. Other targets in September included a Fortune 500 hospitality company, a major US airline, and a large private US industrial supplies distributor. These attackers stole sensitive data and credit card records using Cairn and two other open source AI tools. The incidents highlight a growing trend of using autonomous agents to conduct complex, multi-stage cyberattacks against diverse global targets.

stories.Headline: Researchers propose sparse rational learning that recovers compact aerodynamic surrogate models
stories.Summary:
The paper "Sparse rational learning for interpretable aerodynamic surrogate modeling" was published in Acta Mechanica Sinica on 19 November 2026, with its abstract posted on Springer Nature Link at 06:00 UTC. The work proposes sparse rational learning, called SRL, for aerodynamic surrogate modeling. SRL first converts the non-convex rational regression problem into a linear system through algebraic linearization. It then applies sparse optimization to recover a compact rational expression from the candidate library. The paper develops two sparse solution algorithms, a fast relaxation method based on the L1-norm called L1-SRL and an exact solution method based on mixed-integer programming and the L0-norm called L0-SRL.

Results from a dozen mathematical benchmark tests show that the L1 algorithm carries a risk of fitting divergence for certain rational structures. The L0 algorithm maintains excellent robustness and recovers all polynomial and rational functions. On the Laboratory Technology Vehicle aerodynamic dataset, SRL variants produce compact rational expressions that outperform polynomial surrogates and gplearn. Those expressions remain competitive with state-of-the-art symbolic regression at moderate to high complexity. The paper further introduces two practical extensions to improve noise robustness and fitting performance, clarifies the methodological distinctions between SRL- and SINDy-based methods, and compares their performance.

The paper states that accurate and interpretable aerodynamic prediction is crucial for the design and control of modern flight vehicles. It says established surrogate approaches including kriging, radial basis functions, support vector machines, and deep neural networks achieve high predictive accuracy but do not yield explicit interpretable mathematical formulas. Among interpretable surrogate models, it says polynomial regression is inadequate for strongly nonlinear aerodynamic responses. It says symbolic regression is more powerful but relies on stochastic search and may yield deeply nested expressions that compromise interpretability. It says rational functions strike a good balance between accuracy and interpretability, making them well suited for aerodynamic surrogate modeling, but fitting a full rational function directly from data risks overfitting due to its large number of candidate coefficients and terms.

The paper states that the source code supporting the study is publicly available at https://github.com/ctluo/SparseRationalLearning.jl. It states that the Laboratory Technology Vehicle aerodynamic dataset analyzed in the study is a publicly available benchmark dataset released by the AIAA Applied Aerodynamics Surrogate Modeling Working Group, as cited in the manuscript. It states that the mathematical benchmark data, noise robustness data, and genuine pole benchmark data were generated from the analytical expressions, sampling domains, sampling procedures, and random seeds described in the manuscript and accompanying code. It states that no additional proprietary or experimental data were generated for this study. The reference list includes Bekemeyer, Hariharan, Wissink, et al., in Introduction of applied aerodynamics surrogate modeling benchmark cases: Proceedings of AIAA SCITECH 2025 Forum, Orlando, 2025, AIAA Paper 2025-0036.

The reference list includes Queipo, Haftka, Shyy, Goel, Vaidyanathan, and Tucker, Surrogate-based analysis and optimization, Prog. Aerospace Sci. 41, 1 (2005). It includes Kou and Zhang, Data-driven modeling for unsteady aerodynamics and aeroelasticity, Prog. Aerospace Sci.

125, 100725 (2021). It includes Shyy, Cho, Du, Gupta, Tseng, and Sastry, Surrogate-based modeling and dimension reduction techniques for multi-scale mechanics problems, Acta Mech. Sin. 27, 845 (2011). It includes Li and Luo, A rational learning method for aerodynamic modeling, Aerospace Sci.

Tech. 177, 112945 (2026). It includes Petersen and Øiseth, Bayesian rational function models for aerodynamic derivatives of parametrized bridge decks, Adv. Wind Eng. 3, 100102 (2026).

The reference list includes Tibshirani, Regression shrinkage and selection via the Lasso, J. R. Statistical Soc. Ser. B-Statistical Methodology 58, 267 (1996). It includes Bertsimas, King, and Mazumder, Best subset selection via a modern optimization lens, Ann. Statist.

44, 813 (2016). It includes Willis and von Stosch, L0-constrained regression using mixed integer linear programming, Chemometrics Intelligent Lab. Syst. 165, 29 (2017). It includes Brunton, Proctor, and Kutz, Discovering governing equations from data by sparse identification of nonlinear dynamical systems, Proc.

Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 113, 3932 (2016). It includes Kaheman, Kutz, and Brunton, SINDy-PI: a robust algorithm for parallel implicit sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics, Proc.

R. Soc. A. 476, 20200279 (2020). The paper states that the framework provides a practical, lightweight, and interpretable tool for aerodynamic surrogate modeling. The articles leave open the details of the two practical extensions beyond their stated aims of improving noise robustness and fitting performance.

They leave open the specifics of the comparison between SRL- and SINDy-based methods beyond the statement that distinctions are clarified and performance compared. They leave open the full contents of the mathematical benchmark data, noise robustness data, and genuine pole benchmark data beyond their described generation. They leave open the full reference list beyond the entries shown. They leave open the manuscript's account of the AIAA Applied Aerodynamics Surrogate Modeling Working Group citation.

stories.Headline: Researchers propose symmPINN to improve training of physics-informed neural networks on singular perturbation problems
stories.Summary:
Researchers proposed a new method called symmPINN to improve the training of physics-informed neural networks on singular perturbation problems. This work was published in Acta Mechanica Sinica on November 19, 2026. The authors developed this approach to solve singularly perturbed thin-boundary-layer differential equations. They aimed to fix training difficulties caused by rapid variations in boundary layers. This new system enhances training efficiency for these specific mathematical challenges.

The method requires a mirror extension strategy to symmetrically extend the computational domain. This process relocates the boundary layers to the interior of the extended domain. It enforces virtual symmetry constraints so the solution becomes centrally symmetric around the original boundary-layer position. The researchers tested this on single-sided and double-sided boundary layer problems. They also applied it to laminar flow through a channel with a porous wall and thin plate bending.

The authors stated that standard physics-informed neural networks encounter training difficulties due to rapid variations in boundary layers. They explained that symmetry constraints help mitigate gradient angle conflicts between differential equation and boundary condition losses. They noted that these two losses originally have a gradient angle cosine of approximately minus one. By reducing this conflict, the symmPINN approach improves the overall training efficiency. The researchers claim the system exhibits superior performance across various typical singular perturbation problems.

The researchers found that the gradient angle analysis proves the effectiveness of the virtual symmetry constraints. These constraints specifically benefit the training of neural networks when dealing with steep boundary layers. The affected problems include classic cases like the thin plate bending problem. These mathematical issues typically involve rapid changes that confuse standard deep learning frameworks. The symmPINN method provides a more stable way to handle these sharp transitions.

The background involves physics-informed neural networks, which are deep learning frameworks for solving nonlinear partial differential equations. Previous research by Raissi, Perdikaris, and Karniadakis in 2019 established the foundation for these networks. Other scholars have explored domain decomposition and variational approaches to solve similar physical problems. The study references boundary layer theory and asymptotic methods from authors like Schlichting, Kestin, Bender, and Orszag. It also builds on work regarding the large deflection of circular clamped plates by W. Z. Chien.

The researchers demonstrated that symmPINN performs better than standard methods for thin-boundary-layer differential equations. The articles show the method works for both single-sided and double-sided boundary layers. Future applications may include more complex fluid mechanics or elasticity problems. The text does not specify if this method can be applied to all types of differential equations. It leaves open whether other symmetry strategies could further improve the training of these networks.

stories.Headline: Unsiloed AI raises $7.5M seed to help enterprises make complex documents usable by AI agents
stories.Summary:
Unsiloed AI has raised $7.5 million in seed funding led by Felicis to help enterprises make complex documents usable by AI agents, TechGig reported on November 19, 2026. The San Francisco-headquartered startup addresses the problem of AI systems misinterpreting tables, charts, and complicated layouts in business documents, which can cause costly mistakes in banking, healthcare, and legal services. Its software breaks down complex documents, extracts information from elements like tables and charts, and converts it into structured data that AI agents can use. The technology also shows the origin of extracted information in the original document so businesses can verify results. Co-founders Aman Mishra and Adnan Abbas, former classmates at IIT Kharagpur, joined Y Combinator's Fall 2025 batch after developing the technology.

Unsiloed uses "dual-stream" vision models that process text and image data separately, along with "heat map-based chunking" to identify key parts of a document, directing more computing power toward figures, numbers, and charts. A specialized decoder considers industry-specific terminology to distinguish terms with different meanings in various business contexts. In a test involving 542 financial documents from an enterprise customer, Unsiloed achieved 99.78 per cent accuracy across approximately 84,000 extracted data points, compared with major AI models, Microsoft's Azure Document Intelligence, and the customer's in-house tool, though the results have not been independently verified. Unsiloed claims it outperformed competing tools on olmOCR-Bench, a public benchmark by Allen AI, scoring 88.0 in startup-conducted tests against Reducto's 66.0 and Unstructured's 39.9 across 1,403 PDF pages. Mishra, co-founder and CEO, said large language models are inherently probabilistic and can induce deviation or hallucination, which can have a massive negative impact downstream.

He said Unsiloed is working with customers in finance, legal services, and healthcare, including one bank processing documents and a law firm that deployed it on its own servers for contracts and old case files. He also named voice AI startup Bolna AI as a customer, which uses Unsiloed to ingest knowledge bases for building voice agents. Mishra said pricing starts at one cent per page, and he asserted the approach reduces costs by focusing computing power on critical document sections. Unsiloed, with a team of seven, plans to use the funding to hire more researchers and engineers, expand sales, and develop proprietary datasets.

stories.Headline: CISOs expect 60% to let AI agents act autonomously on low-risk security tasks within a year
stories.Summary:
Security leaders are about to hand AI agents a lot more authority, according to a recent a16z survey of CISOs at organizations with more than 1,000 employees. In that survey, 36% said they are comfortable today letting AI agents act autonomously on low-risk security actions. In 12 months from now, 60% expect to be comfortable at that level. Overall, AI SOC was the highest ranking initiative for 2027. The Hacker News published the article on Nov 20, 2026.

The same survey found the most common worry was AI-accelerated attacks outpacing the team's ability to respond, selected by 55% of respondents. Only 1% are comfortable with agents acting autonomously on most actions today, and only 7% expect to be a year from now. According to the a16z survey, 52% of CISOs want agents to act only with human approval. In the a16z survey, 46% of CISOs listed AI agents acting outside their intended permissions, or compromised agents, among their five biggest worries, and 29% cited prompt injection or data leakage through AI applications. Meanwhile 55% already run MCP servers or other agent-to-application integrations in production, and 34% run autonomous agents with tool access or write permissions.

In a widely cited 2000 paper, Parasuraman, Sheridan and Wickens proposed that automation applies to four broad functions. Those are information acquisition, information analysis, decision and action selection, and action implementation. Each function can sit at a different level of automation, from fully manual to fully automatic, within the same system. Researchers at the University of Washington define five levels of agent autonomy by the role the human plays. The authors make a point every SOC leader should take to heart, that autonomy is a deliberate design choice, separate from how capable the agent is.

Gartner offers a complementary distinction between a human in the loop, who approves each action, and a human on the loop, whose oversight is strategic. The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications extends least privilege into least agency, granting agents only the minimum autonomy needed for safe, bounded tasks. Read through this lens, the a16z data describes a market moving from roughly L2 today toward L4 for low-risk actions within a year. The article says analyst time is the scarcest resource in the SOC, and every alert still means pulling evidence from several systems, reconstructing what happened and deciding whether it matters.

The article maps the four stages onto security operations as evidence collection, analysis and verdict, response recommendation, and response execution. It says a team can automate the first two stages heavily, since that is where analyst hours go and where mistakes are cheapest to catch. The same team can stay conservative on the fourth stage, where a wrong move disrupts the business. As the a16z report itself puts it, gathering logs is different from changing a production system. The article says the exact placement will differ by organization, and that is the point.

The article says the move from 36% to 60% will happen with or without a plan. It lists five steps, starting with inventorying every action and placing each one on the reversibility, blast radius and receipts rubric. It says to automate investigation aggressively, gate disruptive response with real evidence, write graduation and demotion criteria now, and govern the agent like a privileged identity. It says a single serious miss should trigger a demotion until the criteria are met again. The article ends mid-sentence, describing forensic-level investigation as the approach Intezer's AI SOC is bui.

stories.Headline: Chinese hackers use Cairn AI tool to find zero-day vulnerability and breach East Asian universities
stories.Summary:
Chinese hackers used an autonomous AI penetration-testing framework called Cairn to breach several universities in East Asia. Amazon's Threat Intelligence team discovered this activity on September 10, 2026, after finding a publicly accessible server hosting the tool. The attackers used Simplified Chinese prompts and China Standard Time to coordinate multiple AI agents toward gaining shell access. These agents operated continuously for 16 hours without breaks, executing thousands of actions to find a way into the systems.

The attack required the AI to identify a path traversal vulnerability in an open-source medical imaging AI application. Amazon assesses with high confidence that this was a zero-day because no prior security advisory or fix existed in vulnerability databases. The hackers used this specific flaw to breach two different universities after failing to exploit Log4Shell or guess 30,000 credential combinations. Amazon subsequently contacted the application maintainers to fix the bug and worked with a government partner to notify the victims.

CJ Moses, the CISO of Amazon Integrated Security, stated that the AI agents planned and adjusted their approach without the operator choosing every step. He warned that agents discovering zero-days in minutes can complete activities faster than security operations centers can manually triage alerts. Moses noted that the speed and operational tempo of these autonomous tools make them particularly dangerous for targeted organizations. He highlighted that the tool is ideal for attackers because it can coordinate complex tasks using only plain language objectives.

This incident follows recent warnings from the FBI and Google regarding other AI-backed offensive tools like Artex, CyberStrikeAI, and PentAGI. Artex has been linked to attacks on Japanese and South Korean financial institutions and a supply chain attack on ConnectWise. Eyal Sela of Gambit Security noted that Cairn is especially significant because it is a general-purpose tool with less predictable problem-solving structures. Google researchers also observed Cairn being used to target companies within the United States aerospace sector.

stories.Headline: Philip Walton finds AI models pass about 50 per cent of modern web development checks
stories.Summary:
Philip Walton reported that AI models, including the latest frontier versions, pass only about 50 per cent of the checks in an evaluation suite for modern web development, according to TechGig on November 19, 2026. The failures cluster in accessibility, user experience, performance and security, areas web developers deal with daily. The pass rate rises to around 90 per cent when a tool called Modern Web Guidance is used. That guidance is meant to put web platform expertise, best practices and browser compatibility data directly into coding agents, and developers can install it to address the gaps. The accessibility errors include weak keyboard focus and inert management, with models often failing to move focus into new views or restore it correctly.

Models also miss reduced-motion support, such as checking for prefers-reduced-motion in newer features like view transitions. For form validation, they frequently rebuild the CSS :user-invalid behaviour in custom JavaScript, which flags required fields too early, and they misplace format hints that mobile keyboards can obscure. On user experience, agents often use imperative JavaScript for swipe and touch gestures instead of native CSS Scroll Snap, and they fall back on JavaScript workarounds for dialogs, popovers and top-layer transitions instead of modern HTML and CSS features. Dark mode also shows gaps, with models often missing color-scheme settings or the CSS light-dark() function, which can leave native controls in light mode or cause a white flash on page load.

Performance problems include poor main-thread responsiveness, because models often roll custom setTimeout() queues instead of prioritising tasks with scheduler.postTask(). They build complex layouts without content-visibility:auto, causing full-page reflows, and they omit explicit width and height attributes on elements, which affects Cumulative Layout Shift. They also struggle with web font swaps and mobile browser toolbar changes. On security, the concerns include fragile custom DOM XSS sanitizers and permissive Trusted Types policies, and models rarely add Content Security Policy headers without explicit prompting.

Passkey sign-in implementations are often incorrect, with models hand-rolling Base64URL conversion helpers instead of using built-in serialization methods, and they omit PublicKeyCredential.signalUnknownCredential() for unknown credentials. The article attributes the findings to Philip Walton and names Modern Web Guidance as the fix that lifts pass rates from about 50 per cent to around 90 per cent. It does not say when the evaluation was run, how many models or checks were involved, or who publishes the guidance. The article also does not say what happens next beyond noting that developers can install Modern Web Guidance to address the gaps.

stories.Headline: AI-driven bug reports strain Microsoft security and cause system instability
stories.Summary:
Security researchers began flooding Microsoft with a massive volume of bug reports starting in April 2026. This surge in discoveries is driven by the use of artificial intelligence to find vulnerabilities in software. While these bugs are often of relatively low severity, the sheer quantity is straining traditional security defenses. This trend has created a situation where adversaries can adopt new technology faster than defenders can respond.

The current volume of reports is overwhelming the Microsoft Active Protections Program, which has operated for nearly two decades. Since January 2021, Microsoft has issued patches for approximately 10,319 common vulnerabilities and exposures. The scale of the problem is evident in the data, as 2025 saw a total of 1,180 such vulnerabilities. In contrast, 2026 has already seen 5,383 releases, with 5,128 of those occurring since April.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella addressed these challenges during the New York Times DealBook Summit and on CNBC this Wednesday. He explained that while artificial intelligence helps the company find and fix bugs, the resulting flood of patches creates instability. Nadella noted that applying these numerous fixes to older infrastructure makes systems less stable. He clarified that a recent Microsoft 365 outage was caused by a latent bug rather than a direct AI attack.

The Microsoft Security Response Center manages these efforts through the Software and Services Incident Response Plan, which dates back to 2004. This organization coordinates with partner companies to provide early access to bug information before the monthly Patch Tuesday releases. In 2025, Microsoft stopped giving early access to Chinese companies following suspected leaks related to SharePoint attacks. Experts now worry that these established patch programs cannot adapt to the current AI-driven deluge of reports.

stories.Headline: AI may eliminate jobs but children can still thrive, report says
stories.Summary:
The CNN article dated November 20, 2026, discusses how artificial intelligence may eliminate jobs, but argues that today's children can still thrive in an uncertain future. The piece was published by CNN on its website at that date and time. It addresses parents and educators who are concerned about how rapid technological change will affect the next generation. stories.Headline: Chrome DevTools adds AI-assisted Lighthouse audits and offline heap snapshot analysis in December update
stories.Summary:
Chrome DevTools received a December 2026 update that incorporates new features from Chrome 157 and Chrome 158, according to TechGig, which published its report on November 19, 2026. The update enhances debugging capabilities, AI assistance, and performance analysis for web developers. The DevTools MCP server now supports logpoint debugging and virtual WebAuthn authenticators, letting developers inject logpoints at script URLs to log expressions without pausing execution. Developers can also configure virtual authenticators to test passkey and security key flows, and the server offers live configuration reloading and automatic discovery of configuration files. Offline and paginated heap snapshot analysis is now available, allowing inspection of .heapsnapshot files without an active browser connection.

Parallel tool execution across different pages and browser-powered screencasts at device pixel resolution are also new. AI assistance has been upgraded to run full multi-category Lighthouse reports covering performance, accessibility, best practices, and SEO, and it supports agentic-browsing audits with structured summaries of failing audits. The Elements panel now allows forcing :buffering and :stalled media states for testing loading and playback fallback styles, and it includes an interactive swatch for position-try-fallbacks and improved CSS cascade accuracy. The Sources panel supports ECMA-426 source map scopes, displaying original variable and function names in the Scope view, stack traces, and expression evaluation, so developers can debug with authored names instead of minified identifiers. The Application panel adds Sub apps inspection for multi-app web installations and Spellcheck custom dictionary inspection.

The Performance and Memory panels feature faster trace parsing, Lantern HTTP/3 simulation, and heap snapshot context analysis for generators and async functions. Other improvements include accurate UTF-8 byte lengths for WebSocket connections in the Network panel, enhanced text copying in the Console, and Device Mode screenshots that now copy images directly to the clipboard. The articles do not name who is responsible for the update or include any statements from the people behind it. They also do not describe what happens next beyond the features rolling out from Chrome 157 and Chrome 158.

stories.Headline: Black Duck finds organisations close one vulnerability for every 18 they discover
stories.Summary:
Black Duck's 2027 AI Readiness Report found that organisations discovered 18 new vulnerabilities for every one they closed in May 2026, a ratio up from 11-to-1 in June 2025 that peaked at 22-to-1 in December. The report drew on 65,521,627 findings from 13,127 applications at 533 organisations between June 2025 and May 2026. By the end of the study period, only about 10.5 per cent of findings had been closed. In April 2026 alone, organisations added 10.4 million unresolved findings to their backlogs.

The average span between a vulnerability's disclosure and its first exploit has fallen from 2.6 years in 2018 to under one day, a trend the report says frontier AI models accelerated. Median closure times varied by testing method: flaws found in proprietary code through static application security testing took 28 days to close, and open-source vulnerabilities identified via software composition analysis took 39 days. Findings from dynamic testing and manual testing took significantly longer, at 316 and 232 days respectively. Critical-severity open-source issues took 58 days to close while high-severity ones took 22 days, which the report says suggests teams may be fixing easier issues first rather than the most dangerous.

Open source and third-party components accounted for 52 per cent of all critical and high-severity vulnerabilities in the dataset, and among all SCA-identified vulnerabilities only 15 per cent were closed. Organisations running SCA scans 10 to 29 times a month closed open-source vulnerabilities in an average of 30 days, compared to 66 days for less frequent scanning. Black Duck recommends a three-layer approach of deterministic testing, AI-assisted triage and agentic remediation. Greg Hughes, CEO of Black Duck, said organisations must find, prioritise and fix at machine speed, using trusted deterministic testing, AI and agentic remediation.

stories.Headline: VeroSecurity raises $11 million to automate AI policy enforcement for enterprises
stories.Summary:
VeroSecurity, a company founded in 2025, has secured $11 million in seed funding led by TLV Partners, according to a TechGig report published on November 19, 2026. The firm is developing an AI Security Engineering platform that automates policy enforcement for AI tools and agents used inside companies. The platform is meant to address the emerging discipline of securing AI systems within enterprises, which the company says differs from traditional cybersecurity. The funding will support advancement of the platform and help grow VeroSecurity's go-to-market presence in the United States. The platform converts security team policy definitions into enforced controls and automatically updates those controls as AI tools evolve.

Its core technology, the AI Runtime Governor, puts security decisions into effect as AI operates, enforcing approved policies and blocking agent actions that trigger unauthorized behavior. The system refers only enforcement decisions requiring human judgment to security teams, and it brings analysis and recommended actions to security professionals for new risk decisions. VeroSecurity is also establishing AISecurityEngineering.org, an open community and knowledge center offering practical field guides, workshops, and an ASE credential track. Elad Tessler, Co-Founder and CEO of VeroSecurity, told SecurityWeek that the company's own weekly count of open roles titled AI Security Engineer went from 367 on October 25 to 451 on November 14, a rise of 23 percent in three weeks. He said demand is arriving before the discipline has been formally defined, and that established security disciplines grew shared knowledge before standard job titles.

Tessler explained that the Vero platform aims to automate the impossible part of ASE work, including managing dozens of tool changes weekly and ensuring defenses are in place before agents act in seconds. He said the platform leaves the human engineer in place to make judgement calls where necessary, and that VeroSecurity is betting on more AI security engineers, not fewer. Tessler noted that without Vero, keeping up with AI in a large company requires a team, while with the platform one person or a security leader can stay ahead. The company is building AISecurityEngineering.org to train these professionals, according to the report. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the funding supporting platform advancement and US go-to-market growth.

stories.Headline: Booking.com details a 20-year AI platform now serving 400 billion daily predictions
stories.Summary:
Booking.com has detailed a 20-year effort to scale its data and machine learning infrastructure, according to Jabez Eliezer Manuel, in a report published by TechGig on November 19, 2026. The company said the platform now handles 400 billion daily predictions in support of billions of travel decisions. It began with Perl and Postgres, then quickly replaced Postgres with MySQL because of asynchronous replication capabilities. By 2015 Booking.com ran one of the world's largest MySQL clusters, with more than 7,000 instances, using small databases for fast point queries and response times under 350 microseconds. The company also contributed upstream to MySQL, proposing features such as GTID-based replication.

Hadoop was introduced in 2011 to manage growing data, with two on-premise clusters for big data analysis and reporting. By 2018 Hadoop showed limitations, including a shared environment, mono-version constraints, lack of GPU support and capacity issues. The migration to cloud was finalised within 1.5 years by 2023, and it involved mapping dependencies and prioritising critical workflows, with 92 per cent of workflows not passing a test of whether someone cares. A custom Scala service for serving ML models, built in 2015, now supports more than 12 model formats and serves 400 billion predictions per day with average latency under 20 milliseconds. Feature engineering went through three attempts before settling on a feature store for pre-computed feature storage and serving through an API, which addressed data and computational parity challenges.

Booking.com employs multiple ML platforms, including GenAI for conversational experiences and smart filters, Content Intelligence for image and text analysis, and Ranking for ordering millions of products. The Ranking platform evolved from simple formulas to personalised ML models, overcoming initial failures caused by Spark memory limitations. Interleaving was introduced to speed up experimentation for ranking models, allowing 10 times more variants than traditional A/B testing for pre-selection before final A/B tests. The company said it is now building foundations for agentic systems and unifying platforms under a single orchestration layer to prevent fragmentation and centralise AI governance.

stories.Headline: Alteryx adds governance experience to Alteryx One for validating AI outputs
stories.Summary:
Alteryx introduced a new governance experience in its Alteryx One platform on Nov. 20, 2026, the company announced from Irvine, Calif. The experience is designed to solve one of enterprise AI's biggest obstacles, which Alteryx describes as ensuring answer validation, reliability, and repeatable outcomes across business operations and financial processes. Alteryx evolved its VURA framework, standing for Visible, Understandable, Repeatable, Auditable, into an active governance experience. Alteryx One surfaces real-time trust signals directly across OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, and Google Gemini chat interfaces. The company said this lets business users validate AI outputs while equipping IT with centralized control and platform oversight.

Alteryx One makes the data, workflows, and logic behind decisions and automations visible to users. The platform lets organizations operationalize repeatable business logic into governed agentic workflows that AI agents can safely reuse and automate at scale. IT defines software development lifecycle processes, versioning controls, and certification criteria, including statuses such as in review, certified, or deprecated. Sensitivity labels include public, internal, PII, or restricted, alongside custom labels such as "AI-Ready" or "Finance-Approved." Alteryx integrates with Google Cloud Knowledge Catalog, formerly Dataplex, Atlan, and Collibra for data lineage.

Ben Canning, Chief Product Officer at Alteryx, said enterprise AI adoption does not fail because models lack intelligence but stalls because of a fundamental trust gap across decisions and operations. He said business leaders hesitate to act when they cannot verify outputs or govern automated workflows. He said Alteryx One provides the business logic layer that pairs clean, trusted data with LLMs and agents. He said the company embeds its VURA framework directly into conversational interfaces and automated enterprise processes. Canning said AI models are incredibly powerful but leaders need verification.

Roan Pilsworth, Data Consultant at Bulien, said organisations often understand the importance of governing underlying data but many overlook the same practices for processes and workflows. Pilsworth said it has become critical to properly manage processes before they reach production as organizations look to accelerate development with AI. Pilsworth said Alteryx assets can be packaged as immutable objects, allowing logic to be locked down. Pilsworth said this ensures changes are traceable and transparent and assets can be shared while maintaining governance. Alteryx said its platform serves analysts, finance teams, operations teams, and business users.

Alteryx cited its "2026 State of Data Analyst: The Rise of Business Logic" report, in which 43% said interpreting and explaining AI insights remains a key barrier. Alteryx said generating insights faster does not always make decisions easier and that the biggest challenge is helping business leaders understand and trust AI-generated outputs. Alteryx said it has over 8,000 customers and describes itself as the agentic analytics and automation company. Alteryx said non-deterministic AI outputs pose a risk to reporting integrity for financial leaders. Alteryx said finance teams can operationalize governed metrics including Annual Recurring Revenue, Customer Lifetime Value, and revenue calculations.

Alteryx One natively integrates into existing enterprise technology stacks by leveraging the Model Context Protocol. It offers a customizable MCP Server or standard plug-ins for OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Microsoft CoPilot, Databricks Genie, and Snowflake CoCo. Alteryx said offloading heavy data processing and calculation logic to governed workflows rather than LLMs can significantly reduce token consumption and execution time. Alteryx said business users can use natural language to generate and interact with transparent visual workflow diagrams and make incremental edits without recreating entire assets. Alteryx said this keeps intermediate AI actions fully visible for supply chain reordering, billing discrepancy reviews, or financial audits.

Alteryx scheduled a live session titled "Trust at the Speed of AI: November 2026 Release Webinar" with its product experts. The session is to demonstrate how Alteryx One grounds conversational AI in governed business logic, visible data lineage, and automated trust signals. Alteryx said the webinar covers the November 2026 release. The articles did not say how many customers have adopted the new governance experience. The articles did not give pricing or a general availability date for the experience.

stories.Headline: Milemarker adds Model Context Protocol so firms connect their own AI tools to its warehoused data
stories.Summary:
Milemarker, an advisor data warehousing provider, announced this month that it has added a new Model Context Protocol for firms on its platform to connect their own AI tools to their Milemarker-housed data, according to an article published on November 20, 2026, by InvestmentNews. The move comes as advisory firm data remains scattered across CRM, custodian, portfolio management software, financial planning platforms and document storage vaults, which makes it hard to get a high-level picture of a client's situation or to run deeper firm-wide analytics. API integrations between software providers have helped only up to a point, because providers are inconsistent about how many integrations they build and how deep those integrations go, with some offering only read-only access while others allow read-and-write access. Several advisor data warehousing providers such as Skience, BridgeFT and Milemarker have risen over the past several years to aggregate data from disparate platforms into a single clean format that firms can plug into through an API.

The announcement raises the question of whether a centralized data warehouse is needed for AI tools to pull their data from, when tools like the recently released Claude for Financial Advisors can connect to an advisor's individual software tools themselves. The article says one potential answer could be consistency of data, since Milemarker may be able to clean a firm's data and resolve inconsistent, incomplete or incorrect records that AI tools might not catch. Milemarker may also have built more and deeper integrations over its years in the data warehouse business, and the article notes that Claude for Financial Advisors currently lists 22 advisor-specific tools it can connect to, whereas Milemarker boasts over 130 integrations. The article adds that there might be value in having a data connection any AI tool can plug into, which is the main purpose of an MCP, so an advisor who later switches to another AI assistant or builds their own would not need to re-establish all the data connections to their individual tools.

The article, written by Ben Henry-Moreland, a Senior Financial Planning Nerd at Kitces.com, says the big question with data warehousing has always been how much extra value there is in centralizing all of a firm's data in one spot, which inevitably gives rise to the temptation to build custom tools to make use of that data. It says it may be easier now to build custom data dashboards with no-code AI tools, but it is also much easier for off-the-shelf AI tools to connect to an advisor's data sources and pull the data in themselves. For firms with truly niche reporting and data-analytics needs that off-the-shelf tools cannot handle, or bespoke tech stacks of lesser-used software that are less likely to have API connections to newer AI tools, the article says a warehouse to pull in and clean the data may be worth it. But as AI tools expand their integration capabilities and the customizability of their interfaces, the article says it might become increasingly difficult to justify paying for a centralized data warehouse for making custom analytics tools when off-the-shelf software can do much of the same thing.

stories.Headline: FBI warns about ARTEX as AI tool lets attackers breach banks in under three hours
stories.Summary:
The FBI issued a FLASH warning six days before the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI about ARTEX, an open-source tool that lets AI agents carry out an intrusion at machine speed, from reconnaissance through data exfiltration. The warning came as GTA VI, the sequel fans waited 13 years for, arrived this week. Some ARTEX attacks reached privileged access in under three hours. The GitHub repository has since been taken down, but copies are still out there. ARTEX has already been used against banks, government agencies, and tech companies.

In 2022, a 17-year-old broke into Rockstar and leaked early GTA VI footage from a hotel room, using an Amazon Fire Stick and a phone. In September, a Binance engineer went through two rounds of interviews for what looked like a great job and downloaded the take-home assignment, which was malware. The FBI blamed North Korea, and Binance puts the theft that followed at about $6.3 billion. A day after Microsoft 365 went down this month, attackers were already exploiting the confusion, sending fake outage notices that cited the real incident number. Adopting a new security approach means a six-month evaluation, a few more months to roll it out, and a pilot that waits for next year's plan.

Asaf Wiener is co-founder and CEO of Mate Security, which sells AI tools for security operations teams, and he previously led core products at Wiz and drove the growth of Microsoft Defender. Wiener wrote that skill, time, and money used to separate a bored teenager from a professional crew, and now a bored teenager with AI can operate like one. He wrote that Rockstar spent 13 years building a game that feels like real life, and in the same stretch real life took on the rules of the game. He wrote that attackers now run on three-hour clocks, while most security programs run on fiscal years. Wiener wrote that the leaders handling this well know the business first, save the caution for what can't be undone, and change in weeks, not quarters.

Wiener wrote that the best attacks don't look like attacks at all, arriving as job offers, invoices, calendar invites, and logins that look almost normal. He wrote that defenders are being asked to move faster and to tell real from fake at the same time. He wrote that security leaders have been burned by tools that promised a lot and broke things in production. He wrote that a team that misreads a signal will shut down its own business over a broken router, while the real attack walks in looking like a job offer. He wrote that the context defense needs, like who owns the server, whether that user really logged in from Lisbon, and what breaks if a system goes offline, lives inside your company.

Wiener wrote that when the first GTA VI trailer came out, half of the internet asked whether it was gameplay or real footage, and corporate security teams ask that every day now. He wrote that fans waited 13 years for GTA VI and the wait dragged on through so many delays that it became a meme. He wrote that when a game takes that long, you'd expect it to feel dated on arrival, but when GTA VI finally arrived this week, the opposite thing happened. He wrote that the real world has started to look a lot like the game. He wrote that Rockstar knows what a bored teenager can do.

Wiener wrote that in GTA players can reload their last save, but security teams don't have that luxury. He wrote that companies that make the right call at machine speed will still be around for the next GTA installment, however long it takes. He wrote that an attack that moves at machine speed doesn't wait for procurement. He wrote that attackers are playing on easy mode, and the defense is stuck on a loading screen. The opinions expressed in the Fortune.com commentary piece are solely the views of its author and do not necessarily reflect the opinions and beliefs of Fortune.

stories.Headline: Connecticut court lets parties use secure AI tools and protects resulting work product in Air-Evac case
stories.Summary:
The United States District Court for the District of Connecticut entered an agreed supplement to a standing protective order in Air-Evac EMS, Inc. v. Aetna Life Insurance Company, No. 3:26-cv-01021, on November 4, 2026, at ECF No. 54. The order came on an unopposed motion under Rule 26(c) and the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act. It permits certain uses of generative AI with designated discovery material and addresses protection of the resulting work. Paragraph 24 generally prohibits uploading designated material to generative-AI tools, subject to two exceptions.

The first exception covers secure electronic discovery platforms accessible only to attorneys working on the action, and the second covers enterprise generative-AI tools that do not train on or retain submitted data and do not disclose data to third parties. Uploads outside those exceptions constitute third-party disclosures under the order. Outputs derived from designated material and generated through permissible AI tools receive express work-product treatment. The protection extends to prompts, queries, instructions, inputs, outputs, logs, model or tool settings and similar materials created by or for a party, counsel, litigation support providers, consultants or experts in connection with the action, and it expressly includes materials used in expert work.

Paragraph 24 preserves disclosures required by Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(a)(2) and the court's authority to order disclosure for good cause. It does not impose a separate advance notice or certification requirement for AI use. The order gives parties a concrete way to address concerns that AI-assisted litigation work will generate new demands for prompts, logs and intermediate outputs, while avoiding treatment of the work-product designation as an absolute answer to requests involving expert testimony. The order identifies the Harvey and Legora AI agents as examples but makes no findings about a particular subscription, configuration or vendor's compliance.

The court's entry of the agreement supplies enforceable terms for this litigation, and it does not establish a general AI privilege or determine the admissibility of AI-assisted expert work. The supplement separately addresses protected health information at paragraph 22 and preserves obligations imposed by law and other agreements, including past duties of confidentiality, at paragraph 27. The article recommends that counsel and the vendor identify retention and access practices before agreeing to categorical restrictions, since a promise not to train a model on submitted data does not necessarily satisfy a separate prohibition on retaining that data. It also recommends defining the treatment of prompts, outputs, logs and settings alongside permitted uses, establishing how counsel and experts will identify materials subject to disclosure, determining where necessary AI records may be preserved consistently with preservation duties, and confirming before an upload that the proposed use complies with health information, contractual and other confidentiality obligations.
