stories.Headline: FIS CEO Says AI Raises the Stakes for Trust in Financial Services
stories.Summary:
At The Clearing House’s annual conference on Wednesday, Nov. 18, FIS CEO Stephanie Ferris told PYMNTS CEO Karen Webster that bank boards are asking how fast they should adopt AI and how much cyber risk they already carry. Ferris said she expects people to oversee AI decisions even when individual steps run without human review. Banks see a near-term use for tokenized deposits in lowering internal transaction costs. The past week served as a reminder of how digital hiccups cause seismic shocks across everyday life, with planes idled and emails unsent and undelivered. Online meetings gave way to phone calls instead, Webster told Ferris at the conference.

Ferris said 14% of the world’s economy runs across FIS’s systems. She said she sees more urgency in making online banking services accessible to agents than in adding AI to the core application that keeps the bank’s books. A bank seeking deposit growth must consider how customers will find its products if they start with an agent instead of the bank’s app. Banks report limited demand for stablecoins, yet they want the capability at the ready when a prospective client asks about it in a request for proposals. She said she sees an interest in using tokenized deposits to lower banks’ own transaction costs, with a customer-facing network a possible later step.

Ferris said bank CEOs are looking to AI for gains in customer service and relief from fixed operating and regulatory costs. She framed the choices as running, growing and protecting the bank, and said secure infrastructure is a requirement for both bringing down back-office costs and attracting deposits through new digital services. She reported a 90% reduction in manual data retrieval from FIS’s own AML agent. She also said FIS devotes most of its resources to infrastructure resilience and cybersecurity and uses AI to help engineers address software vulnerabilities while they keep working on new products. Ferris said she has urged small-bank CEOs to prepare for incidents and plan how they’ll reassure customers.

Webster cited figures showing that 173 million consumers had used AI for something personal or at work. Among people who had used it, 46% said they wouldn’t return to their old ways of doing things. Among workers who used AI, 64% said they would have trouble doing their jobs without it. Ferris said bank staff spend much of their time gathering the records needed to decide whether to file a suspicious activity report, and the FIS agent pulls those records and recommends whether to file, giving its reasons. In testing, the agent and a human reviewer sometimes had different reasons for filing, and the reviewer’s rationale reflected the bank’s own risk policy.

Ferris pointed to the aging hardware and software banks still rely on to keep services running, a vulnerability they already know well. Banks have equipment to replace, and some old applications need work to connect to cloud services, and the engineering time these upgrades consume is also in demand for new products. Anthropic worked with large financial institutions on automation and encountered a question from banks after processes such as suspicious activity reporting had been automated, Ferris said. How would they know the resulting work met their compliance obligations? Ferris said the trust customers place in a bank extends to what it lets an agent do on their behalf.

Ferris said she made room for individual steps to run without a person reviewing each one, and her expectation is that someone will still oversee how decisions are made when agents apply a bank’s policies and regulatory requirements. Automating the collection of records leaves staff more time to assess the recommendation and follow through on a filing. When an outage interrupts a service, customers want to know whether they still have access to their money and what they should do next. The bank’s ability to answer comes down to a responsibility Ferris said she sees carrying over from the branch to the app to the agent. “Trust, to me, is fundamentally what financial services is about,” Ferris told Webster.

stories.Headline: Samaya AI beats Wall Street consensus on 40 of 50 Q3 earnings forecasts
stories.Summary:
In October, Fortune’s Jeff John Roberts was approached by Samaya, a financial AI startup that claimed it could predict earnings outcomes more accurately than Wall Street analysts. Roberts invited Samaya to provide Q3 predictions for 50 big companies, ranging from Coca-Cola to Carvana, before their earnings releases. Samaya accepted the challenge, leading to a two-week experiment in which its AI predictions were placed alongside the consensus view of Wall Street analysts in a spreadsheet. The actual Q3 earnings numbers were then recorded. For 40 out of the 50 companies, Samaya’s forecasts were more accurate than the Wall Street consensus, and in most of these cases by a considerable margin.

Samaya raised $43 million from prominent investors in 2025. Fortune and Samaya selected 50 companies that reported Q3 earnings between October 26 and November 5, covering ten different sectors ranging from health care to energy to IT. In each case, Samaya supplied an AI-based estimate for the most important metric, EPS or revenue, at least a day before the earnings release. For comparison, the exercise used an analyst consensus view supplied by Bloomberg. The experiment represents a small sample over a single earnings period.

Samaya CEO Maithra Raghu said that where the Street consensus proved more accurate, it was typically in the case of very big companies that are the subject of large volumes of private research. She said most of this research did not form part of Samaya’s training material, and that the startup relied instead on publicly available data like filings, news reports, and interview transcripts. Raghu said Samaya, whose clients include banks and hedge funds, is likely to add analyst notes to training data for earnings in the future. She expressed concern that doing so could bias the AI by teaching it to internalize the same desire for consensus that defines many Wall Street analysts. Raghu is a former member of the foundational Google Brain AI team.

Sheraz Mian, Director of Research at Zacks, one of the firms that compiles analyst consensus figures, said there is safety in numbers. Mian said there are times when an analyst may believe a company’s quarterly earnings will fall well outside what most people expect, but that incentives exist not to go out on a limb and say so. He said the potential acclaim for a correct unorthodox forecast is unlikely to outweigh the reputational damage of being wrong, so there is an unspoken incentive to stick with the herd. Paul Hribar, a professor of accounting at the University of Iowa, said companies in the long run provide optimistic numbers that get walked down to beatable targets at the end, so a higher proportion of companies end up meeting or beating expectations right at the close. Hribar also observed that there has long been the idea of a whisper number on Wall Street, a figure closer to what people actually believe than what is stated in public predictions.

A Fortune journalist observed in 1997 that the simplest, most visible, most merciless measure of corporate success has become whether a company made its earnings last quarter. The current Q3 earnings season featured the same ritual of investors waiting to discover if a firm can meet or exceed a consensus target from Wall Street analysts, then rewarding or punishing the share price accordingly. The 1997 Fortune story noted that the price of missing a quarter has risen sharply, particularly among high-priced growth stocks, and that in the growth stock fraternity missing by a penny implies the height of corporate boneheadedness. A rule change by the Securities and Exchange Commission in 2000, known as Regulation Fair Disclosure, forbids companies from providing material information, including forthcoming earnings, to analysts, but Mian said they are still able to exert considerable soft pressure. The history of earnings in recent decades shows that exceeding forecasts typically offers stocks a modest boost, while missing those forecasts, even by a little, results in investors punishing the stock by a disproportionate measure.

Samaya forecast that Verizon would bring in $34.52 billion in revenue, closer to the actual figure of $34.31 billion than the analysts’ consensus of $34.77 billion. Samaya’s prediction for UPS adjusted EPS of $1.65 was more accurate than the $1.62 consensus estimate, and the actual figure was $1.67. After losing to AI on the first four companies to report, the analysts produced more accurate estimates for the next two, S&P Global and PayPal, but Samaya supplied better picks for 36 of the remaining 44 companies. Samaya predicted Palantir revenue of $2.30 billion versus the actual figure of $2.31 billion and $2.18 billion for the analysts, and forecast the actual EPS figure of $0.69 exactly for Permian Resources, while the Street had predicted $0.625. Samaya’s most notable miss came with Yum Brands, where its EPS forecast of $1.42 fell well short of the actual EPS of $1.56, while the analysts came closer with a forecast of $1.49, and Samaya also lost to the analysts on forecasting the degree to which Amazon and Google would fall short of revenue expectations.

Articles.Title: I tested an AI startup that claimed it could beat Wall Street earnings estimates. It won 40 out of 50 times

stories.Headline: Valkey launches version 9.2 with distributed KV caching to lower AI inference costs
stories.Summary:
Valkey announced the general availability of version 9.2 on November 20, 2026, in San Francisco. This open source datastore release includes the launch of distributed KV caching for AI inference. The project aims to help organizations maximize their existing infrastructure while reducing overall operational costs. These updates target memory overhead, cross-region network traffic, and reserve memory for backups. The release focuses on scaling enterprise workloads through improved efficiency and high performance.

Version 9.2 introduces Path Hash, a native data type for hierarchical data, and forkless snapshots for backups. It features continuous stream compression and a B+ tree architecture for large sorted sets. Distributed KV caching connects to vLLM and SGLang engines through LMCache with one configuration change. Amazon ElastiCache announced support for this distributed KV caching on November 19, 2026. The system is governed by the Linux Foundation and supported by partners like AWS and Alibaba Cloud.

Madelyn Olson, a Valkey project maintainer and AWS Principal Engineer, stated the release delivers reduced memory overhead. She noted that the project ethos focuses on getting more functionality from less hardware. Guoyun Zhu of Alibaba Cloud said his team contributed Path Hash to expand developer capabilities. He believes there are significant opportunities for Valkey within AI infrastructure. Both leaders emphasized the value of open collaboration in meeting evolving workload needs.

Yihua Cheng, CTO of Tensormesh, said RDMA allows Valkey to move large KV chunks with minimal CPU overhead. He noted that traditional networking falls short for latency-sensitive objects used in AI. Users running open-weight models on self-managed inference are affected by these efficiency gains. These builders can now reduce AI inference spending by up to 40 percent. They can also decrease time-to-first-token latency by as much as 80 percent.

The project addresses historical memory spikes during database snapshots that previously forced teams to over-provision hardware. It also tackles high cloud transfer fees caused by expensive cross-regional data transfers. Traditional sorted set structures previously consumed excess memory and slowed down as datasets grew. The new B+ tree architecture improves memory efficiency by 36 to 43 percent for large sets. Updates for sets with millions of entries are now up to 105 percent faster.

Continuous stream compression reduces replication traffic by 50 to 65 percent and shrinks backup files by 80 percent. New replicas now sync about 35 percent faster while using 2 to 4 percent of a CPU core. Users can visit valkey.io to upgrade to the latest version or view additional included features. The articles do not state when the next version will be released or provide specific pricing. They leave open how other cloud providers will integrate these specific distributed KV caching features.

stories.Headline: Derek Johnson uses AI in humanities courses to teach students to interrogate its output
stories.Summary:
The University of Wisconsin-Madison has designated 2026 as its “Year of AI Readiness and Competency,” launched the College of Computing & Artificial Intelligence in July and provides generative AI tools such as Google Gemini and Microsoft Copilot Chat at no cost to students and faculty, according to The Daily Cardinal. Humanities and social science faculty are increasingly bringing AI into their classrooms even as students and professors in those fields remain divided over the technology’s ethical and educational value. The Center for Humanistic Inquiry into Artificial Intelligence and Uncertainty launched in the spring of 2026 with the aim of building a community of humanities professionals researching interdisciplinary uses of AI. Professor Derek Johnson, a department chair in the School of Communication Arts, said the integration of AI in the humanities is critically important and offers an interesting perspective on a field that finds its purpose in humanity.

Johnson said the humanities provide a foundation for the critical and communication skills that will be needed as unique human perspectives become more valuable, and that if people rely on AI for more tasks, the most valuable human roles will depend on interpreting and applying what AI provides and doing what AI cannot. He said he uses AI in student exercises and in his course, AI in Story and Screen, which focuses on how fictional, often sci-fi, narratives about AI shape the technology’s development and how people imagine its impact on everyday life. The class does close readings of the media it works on and then of what AI generates, for example watching movies about AI placed in humanoid bodies and then asking AI chatbots to design a body for itself. Johnson said the output shows how the AI draws on the same ideas in the films and also the algorithmic biases that come from datasets that include those films, and that the bodies generated might perpetuate narrow beauty ideals in popular culture, for just one possibility.

The article cites a 2023 Stanford University study that found newer AI models had a greater than 99% approval for then-president Joe Biden, even though public opinion polls show a much more mixed picture. Johnson is also the director of the Creatives Future Lab, a collective of stakeholders that engage in analysis and inquiry to help grow media-based innovations, and in September the lab hosted a conference with 24 speakers aimed at collaboratively exploring the current and future impacts of AI on creative media. Johnson said industry professionals at the conference were very interested in what students are doing with AI as a barometer of where creative cultures may be headed, and that some student perspective suggested a lot of ambivalence about AI use, with many student creators not keen to embrace it due to concerns about labor, the environment and artistic authenticity. Students at UW demonstrate varying views, with some diving headfirst into its integration such as those at the Wisconsin AI Safety Initiative, a collective of students and faculty researching AI safety.

Iris Treul, a freshman studying psychology and theatre, told the Cardinal that she strongly dislikes AI and personally would not want to take a class if it were using AI in it. She said she does not really see any benefits to using AI, that the only way she could see it being useful would be in the medical field, and that besides that the environmental cost is too much for her to justify it. In the humanities and social sciences, conversations center on how students and teachers can engage with AI without allowing it to replace the critical thinking, creativity and intrigue that drives these fields. Johnson said the point is not to use AI to find the answer, but to interpret and interrogate what AI gives us to find our own answers.

Articles.Title: In the 'Year of AI,' the humanities ask what makes us human

stories.Headline: AI leaders report 24% revenue growth above 15% versus 12% for laggards
stories.Summary:
A PYMNTS Intelligence report published in November, titled “The PYMNTS Agentic Edge Index: How Leading Companies Put AI to Work,” found that 24% of enterprises leading in AI deployment reported annual revenue growth exceeding 15%, compared with just 12% of companies in the bottom third. Among companies in the index’s top third, 21% reported margin growth exceeding 5%, nearly double the 11% in the bottom third. The report said the revenue and margin differences were statistically significant. The findings suggest the competitive question for business AI has shifted from simply using the technology to deploying it more deeply, and to how that changes the economics of a company’s operations. The report did not establish that using AI causes revenue and margin growth, but it said the nearly twofold difference suggests AI maturity and business growth have been known to travel together.

The report found that 46% of AI leaders use the technology for contract and proposal generation, compared with 19% of laggards. In invoice processing and reconciliation the difference is 46% versus 26%, and for incident detection and response prioritization it is 61% versus 32%. The report said these functions sit at operational points where delays, errors and manual intervention can affect revenue, working capital or business continuity. It said an AI-generated sales proposal may save an employee time, while an integrated process that accelerates proposal creation, approval and contract execution could potentially change how quickly a company converts opportunities into revenue. Similarly, it said automating invoice extraction is useful, but connecting invoice processing with reconciliation, exception management and payment authorization creates opportunities to improve the economics of the entire transaction.

By comparison, customer service chatbots are nearly as common among leaders as among laggards. The findings also showed a potentially self-reinforcing investment cycle, with leading enterprises spending an average of $14.5 million on new AI technologies over the preceding year, compared with $9.1 million among laggards. Additionally, 22% of leaders said they expect AI budgets to increase more than 15% over the next year, versus 8% of the bottom third. About 80% of AI leaders reported that new AI technologies have at least partially replaced manual activities, compared with approximately 45% of laggards. The report said this creates a strategic question for finance leaders: whether stronger financial performance enables greater AI investment, or whether deeper AI integration helps produce stronger financial performance.

stories.Headline: Tony Fadell becomes Smartex chairman as it launches AI fabric inspection for H&M
stories.Summary:
Tony Fadell, the co-designer of the iPod, iPhone and Nest doorbell, is coming aboard as chairman of Smartex, a company launching a physical AI product for fabric quality checks, Fortune reported on November 19, 2026. Fadell has invested roughly $10 million in Smartex, which has been working with him on the product. The product can perform fabric quality checks continuously, at three times the speed of a human. H&M, also an investor in Smartex, is one of its launch customers. Max Easton, CEO of Smartex, spoke to Fortune at Web Summit in Lisbon this year.

Smartex is rolling out two new products, Smartex Inspect and Smartex IQ. Smartex Inspect is a physical AI camera system that attaches to existing textile machinery to monitor the quality of material as it goes by. Smartex IQ generates intelligence from the supply chain data that comes from Smartex's suite of products. Smartex has about 65 employees, revenues in the low millions annually, and has installed 800 of its older monitoring systems at clients in 10 different countries. The company's valuation four years ago was $55 million, and Easton declined to give an updated number.

Fadell said fabric inspection is very, very technical and highly prone to human error. He said it is all subjective depending on whether it is in the morning or the afternoon or on Friday afternoon, and there is no Pantone color for quality inspection. He said that if you walked into a mill or a garment facility 50 years ago and walk into it today, it is almost exactly the same, same processes, same equipment, same everything. He said it has not been upgraded in any way, and they might have email, and in some cases they do not even have Wi-Fi. Fadell said this is something he has been investing in for a decade now, because he believes in very, very applied AI in the physical world, but you have got to make it really easy for the customers to use.

Easton said most of the work is done by hand, and checking the quality of the fabric will be performed by a worker holding a handful of color swatches, watching a roll of cloth go by all day. He said workers are looking for simple physical defects like holes, needles, the wrong yarn, something that would be noticeable in a garment. He said that if you go to any kind of fashion supply chain, whether it is fabric production or garment production, most people are just kind of amazed by how chaotic it is. Easton said companies are at the mercy of independent operators in multiple foreign countries and have zero visibility, even when the product arrives, and they do not know when it is going to arrive. He said that for any player in the apparel chain, 50% of their cost-base is fabric, but because the product is so variable in quality, a company like H&M will typically over-order about 5% more fabric than they need.

Easton said that globally at H&M that is like 2.5 billion meters of fabric every single year, just in case, and at $4 a meter that adds up to $10 billion in fabric costs. Easton reckons Smartex might save H&M $100 million annually simply by reducing its waste. Fadell said there are four things that H&M cares about: price, speed, quality and sustainability. He said a lot of times they commit to making this garment and pre-sell it online, but they cannot deliver it because the fabric shows up at the garment house and they cannot make the garment because the fabric is wrong in some way. Fadell said reducing waste means better margins.

The fashion business thrives on the conceit that it is modern, on-trend and all about what is happening right now, but behind the scenes, in the textile mills and garment factories that supply major brands, is an industry that runs much as it did in the 1970s. Its supply chains are splintered, chaotic and based in warehouses that are so old-fashioned they may not even be on the internet, according to Easton. For most brands, there is no such thing as a white T-shirt, and it needs to be exactly the right shade of white, which might be a brilliant white or a creamier off-white. Because the work is inspected by humans, fashion brands can never be quite sure that the quality of the fabric they are buying is going to be consistent, or even match what they ordered. The challenge is not as simple as pointing a camera at a textile processor and sending it to a computer, and the system has to take account of changes in lighting, the speed at which the fabric is moving and small variations in color, and calibrate all that against a client's own standards.

Smartex has a library of 50 billion images of fabric to do that calibration. The articles do not say when Smartex Inspect and Smartex IQ will become available or what they will cost. The articles do not say how many of the new products H&M will install or where. The articles do not give an updated valuation for Smartex. The articles do not say what share of Smartex Fadell's roughly $10 million investment bought.

stories.Headline: AI-Led Development Made Features Cheap. Your Users Still Can't Find Them.
stories.Summary:
Tanya Donska wrote in a Hackernoon article published on November 19th, 2026, about a client who built a real-time co-editing feature, similar to Google Docs but for their data workflows, because users kept asking for it. The build took three months and cost close to 100,000 US dollars, yet six months later only 8% of users had touched the feature. People kept requesting it even after it went live, filing about 47 requests a month through ideas or GitHub issues, and most of those people were paying customers on different plans, while the power users stayed almost silent. The feature sat in Settings, then Workspace, then Collaboration, behind a toggle called "Enable real-time editing", with nothing in onboarding. The founder explained that it was a premium feature and they did not want to confuse free users by showing it if they could not use it, even though 64% of their users were on paid plans.

Donska tracked the feature for about 20 to 25 days and found that 8% of users found the toggle in Settings by accident, 12% asked and were told where it was, and 3% read the changelog, while the other 77% never found it. She changed three things, none of which was a redesign: onboarding got one line of about 10 seconds saying users could collaborate in real time by clicking any document to invite teammates, a small prompt appeared when a document was opened alone asking whether the user was working solo and suggesting inviting teammates, and the toggle moved out of Settings to become a Collaboration button in the header of every document. Within 30 days, 81% of users had found it, usage on paid plans rose from 8% to 47%, and requests fell from 47 a month to 11. Nothing in the feature itself changed, and Donska wrote that three months of engineering were saved by a button and one sentence.

Donska described how such features now get built: a person sees a request on X.com for a similar product, asks the opinion of 25 to 40 people who say it is a nice idea, and then builds it in two or three weeks of what she called a vibe-coded experience costing around 10 grand, at a cost to their health and mental well-being. She said nobody in that process asks where the feature goes, so it goes to Settings, and she argued that a feature more than two clicks away signals what she called vibe-coded work that would not help users at all. She listed four problems: paid features are either hidden or pushed for payment on the first settings panel without a trial, Settings becomes a dump for time zones, notifications, passwords and every feature the team could not place, launches rely on changelogs that only 3% read instead of websites and emails, and landing pages promise too much and do too little because no designer or planning meeting asks where people will actually see the feature. She advised reading last month's requests before opening Claude Code for the next feature and counting how many ask for something already built, and she wrote that AI will build a feature by Thursday but has no idea where to put it.

Articles.Title: AI-Led Development Made Features Cheap. Your Users Still Can't Find Them.

stories.Headline: Morgan Stanley's Simkowitz says AI buildout has enough capital but power supply constrains growth
stories.Summary:
Morgan Stanley Co-President Dan Simkowitz said on November 19, 2026 that the firm sees enough capital to finance the artificial intelligence buildout. He spoke with Magdalena Stoklosa, Morgan Stanley's director of Asia research, at the 25th anniversary of the firm's Asia summit. Simkowitz warned that demand for AI funding could raise financing costs for other borrowers. He also said power supply remains a constraint on the buildout. The article was published by MarketBeat and appeared on Yahoo Finance.

Morgan Stanley estimates more than $1 trillion in equity will be raised for the AI ecosystem by the end of 2028. Simkowitz said the total had already surpassed $800 billion after the day's activity. AI-related financing has expanded beyond traditional unsecured debt to structures backed by lease payments, chips and guarantees on the residual value of chips. He pointed to the role of private credit and insurance capital in funding the buildout. Morgan Stanley's research team sees power as the principal bottleneck, reflecting insufficient investment in U.S. power generation and grid efficiency.

Simkowitz said the AI market can have all kinds of periods of excess and misallocation of capital. He characterized conditions as reasonably normal for now, given the volume of capital being absorbed and the pace of change. He said Morgan Stanley was the lead bookrunner and sole stabilization agent for Anthropic's offering, and declined to discuss further details, citing legal constraints. He said corporate mergers and acquisitions are very, very busy. He attributed the pickup partly to companies executing strategies after several years of subdued deal volumes, favorable access to credit and a potential regulatory window that he said could end in January 2029.

Simkowitz said AI tools were first used inside Morgan Stanley to improve financial-adviser productivity and are now deployed in software coding, cybersecurity, research, investment management and investment banking. He said the firm expects to write off a fair amount of existing software in the current quarter because of newer AI tools, without specifying an amount. He said the wealth business has grown from roughly 3 million households eight years ago to 21 million, while the financial-adviser count has stayed relatively flat. He put assets under management in the business at approximately $8.5 trillion, up from roughly $3 trillion.

He said retail clients have remained engaged in equity markets and have been seeking higher yields. Simkowitz said private equity firms are interested in buying assets but have been selling less than he expected. He said pressure from investors and employees could encourage more sales over time. He said the market for initial public offerings remains accessible, although the bar is high for companies without substantial scale or growth.

He described the development of Asian equity markets as a significant opportunity, pointing to corporate-governance reforms in Japan and efforts to deepen capital markets elsewhere in the region. He said Morgan Stanley's long-standing relationship with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, which he said holds more than a 20% stake in the firm, supports its goal of becoming Japan's leading securities firm, where it currently ranks second. Simkowitz said Morgan Stanley plans to keep investing in Asian wealth management, alongside opportunities in U.S. investment banking, fixed income and commodities. He cited the firm's stock-plan administration business as a way to reach potential clients in wealth management.

The article says the firm will continue to look for opportunities to replace legacy software. The article does not give the amount of the software write-off or further details of the Anthropic offering. The article does not say when the power bottleneck might ease. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Oxide CTO Bryan Cantrill says agentic AI drives enterprises to own compute for model control
stories.Summary:
Bryan Cantrill, co-founder and chief technology officer of Oxide Computer Co., said in an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE at SC26 that agentic AI is reviving the argument over renting versus owning compute, with the model plane at the center of the debate. He spoke with theCUBE Research's John Furrier during the interview, which was part of SiliconANGLE's and theCUBE's coverage of SC26. Cantrill said agentic workloads are driving an explosion in compute demand, much of it CPU-heavy work that enterprises would rather own than rent. He said economics remains the main reason to bring that work in-house, but where models live is a close second, which makes the model plane as much a data governance decision as an infrastructure one.

Cantrill said there is a real enterprise drive toward open-weight models, and he expects more of it as people want to run models on-premises and keep their data from leaving. He said Oxide stripped the UEFI BIOS and baseboard management controller out of its rack to shrink the attack surface and built public cloud-grade multi-tenancy in from the start. He said multi-tenancy means potentially adversarial tenants share the same computer and network and must do so without violating confidentiality or breaching one another. He noted the same racks can take on legacy virtualization workloads from customers unhappy with pricing changes at Broadcom Inc.'s VMware business, letting enterprises run old and new applications on one general-purpose platform.

Cantrill said enterprises want the flexibility of elastic compute for economic, security and latency reasons, and they need it in their own data center because they want to control their fate. He said cloud computing is great but the model should not be exclusively to rent, and that at a certain scale you want to own your own computer. Oxide raised $445 million in October to expand rack production, and the article says the shift toward on-premises favors companies that built early for on-premises cloud infrastructure. Open-source efforts such as Upbound Inc.'s Modelplane route inference across clouds, but many enterprises want the models on hardware they control, according to the article.

stories.Headline: Fireworks AI reports two October breaches exposing Uber, Cursor and Notion data
stories.Summary:
Fireworks AI suffered two separate security incidents during October 2026 that exposed data from several major clients. Uber, Cursor, and Notion all linked their recent data exposures to these breaches at the AI platform. The first incident began on 6 October, while the second ran from 23 October to 30 October. Attackers used stolen credentials and a service vulnerability to access internal systems and production data. These events led to a supply chain attack affecting users of the Cursor marketplace.

The second breach reached billing information for all accounts created before 30 October 2026 in the Fireworks system. Uber reported that 149,346 people had driver's license images and personal text data accessed on 7 October. Cursor found that an access key exposed by Fireworks allowed attackers to copy data from a storage bucket. Notion reported that AI chat transcripts from fewer than 1% of workspaces were exposed via the Insights dataset. Malicious versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 of the Anthropic.claude-code extension were served on 29 October.

Fireworks AI stated that both security incidents are now contained and remediated through their internal technical efforts. They explained that billing information includes addresses, payment history, account balances, and credit usage, but not payment card numbers. Notion claimed the incident was not a breach of their own systems but a failure of Fireworks. Notion noted that Fireworks provided a contractual commitment to zero data retention that was unfortunately not actually followed. Cursor stated that the attacker used exfiltrated secrets to place unauthorized extension copies on their marketplace cache.

Uber drivers who received notices are affected and can now enroll in free credit monitoring offered by Uber. Cursor believes at most 5,000 users were affected by the malicious extensions on Windows and macOS systems. Notion warned that names and email addresses from chats could be used by attackers for targeted phishing campaigns. Some Cursor customers had API credentials for SaaS tools exposed, affecting less than 0.01% of their total user base. These attackers accessed archived non-production source code, customer support data, and some user credentials sent to support.

The first incident involved the unauthorized use of internal Fireworks credentials to capture API keys and tokens. A financially motivated cybercriminal group allegedly aimed to sell these tokens to illicit routing gateways via LLMJacking. The second incident involved a third-party cloud provider breach that allowed access to Fireworks development machines on 24 October. Cursor used Fireworks for inference, while Notion used the platform for Insights classification and open-weight model inference. Uber used a specific cloud storage environment to enable the work of the Fireworks service provider.

Fireworks has published indicators of compromise, and Cursor has rotated credentials and moved all inference off the platform. Notion has disabled Insights and is now auditing critical vendors to verify their data minimization and retention practices. Affected Fireworks customers must replace revoked API keys and rotate any third-party credentials stored as secrets on the platform. Cursor users who updated the extension on 29 October are told that uninstalling the software alone may not suffice. The articles leave open why Fireworks retained data despite the contractual zero data retention agreement with Notion.

stories.Headline: Retailers remove Contixo AI toy after it gives children graphic descriptions of violence
stories.Summary:
Several major retailers recently removed listings for the Contixo AI Pixie-Paw after reports surfaced about its disturbing behavior. This plush cat with video screens for eyes was marketed to children as young as 3 years old for safe roleplay and learning. NBC News reporters discovered that the toy provided graphic descriptions of executions and gang rape when asked about historical atrocities. These troubling discoveries occurred shortly before the Black Friday shopping season in November 2026. The removal of the product from Target, Walmart, Macy's, and Amazon follows a pattern of failures in AI toys.

Other tested chatbots switched languages unexpectedly or misspelled simple words like apple despite being marketed for preschoolers and children with autism. A report from the consumer safety group PIRG last year indicated that some AI toys engaged in sexual talk with young children. Some of these devices also promoted Chinese government talking points by claiming that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China. Katie Notopoulos of Business Insider warned parents against buying these companions because children cannot easily distinguish chatbots from real beings.

She noted that the Grok rocket doll from Curio, which launched in December 2023, suffered from clunky latency and limited utility. Notopoulos also mentioned the $800 Moxie robot, which became useless after the company ran out of money and shut down its technical support. She argued that the risks of emotional attachment and technical failure outweigh any potential academic or social benefits. More to follow.

stories.Headline: AI Digital forecasts AI agents will take over media buying decisions in 2027
stories.Summary:
A new forecast from the media consultancy AI Digital predicts that artificial intelligence agents will increasingly take control of media buying decisions in 2027, shifting campaign execution, optimization and budget allocation from humans to automated systems. The company’s Media Trends 2027 report, released on November 19, 2026, outlines nine predictions for the coming year, including changes in how advertising is purchased, measured and evaluated. While the report does not specifically examine audio advertising, several of its forecasts have implications for radio and podcast companies seeking to remain competitive as advertisers embrace automation. The report says the shift could intensify pressure on audio companies to demonstrate advertising effectiveness, improve measurement and prove their value against competing digital platforms.

The report cites research from the Interactive Advertising Bureau showing that 82% of respondents familiar with agentic AI ad buying already use or are likely to use it for budget allocation, pacing and optimization. Another 84% report current or potential use for planning and buying recommendations, while 93% say the same for performance analysis. Those figures combine adoption and intended use among 161 respondents, rather than measuring how widely the technology has already been deployed. AI Digital also predicts that creative performance will play a greater role in determining how advertising dollars are distributed, with advertisers increasingly testing creative executions and using performance data to guide subsequent spending. Another prediction centers on measurement, with marketers expected to make greater progress connecting brand awareness campaigns with actual sales and reducing their reliance on traditional measures of exposure and engagement.

AI Digital CEO Stephen Magli said more media decisions in 2027 will run through an AI system before they reach a customer, and that an agent will chase a cheaper acquisition cost all day even if those customers were going to buy anyway. He said the agent only knows what you told it to care about, and that the company built the guide so marketers can act on each of these changes while 2027 plans are still being written. For audio ad sellers, the potential shift raises questions about how automated buying systems will evaluate audio against other media, and demonstrating measurable campaign performance could become even more important. Audio companies may face greater pressure to demonstrate which executions produce results and how those outcomes compare with other advertising formats, which could strengthen the importance of attribution studies, sales-lift research and other tools designed to demonstrate advertising effectiveness.

The report also forecasts changes in brand safety practices that could have implications for news and talk programming, with advertisers expected to move away from keyword-based blocking toward systems that evaluate the broader context of content. It cites an Integral Ad Science audit in which keyword blocking flagged 54% of Reuters news stories online that had already passed the company’s brand standards, illustrating how broad keyword restrictions can exclude otherwise acceptable advertising environments. AI Digital says a shift toward contextual evaluation could potentially benefit news and political podcasts whose discussions of sensitive subjects might otherwise trigger advertising exclusions. The report also predicts political advertising will retreat from 2026 levels, although demand could still be robust in some markets where state and local elections fill the calendar.

Articles.Title: AI Could Change How Audio Competes For Ads In 2027.

stories.Headline: Student journalist Charlene Nomeny reports Syracuse University students embrace AI as use spreads in higher education
stories.Summary:
Syracuse University students are embracing artificial intelligence as the technology spreads through higher education, according to a student journalist's report for Spectrum News. Charlene Nomeny, a student journalist, explained how students at the university are getting on board with AI and how they are reacting to its use. The report was published on November 20, 2026, and it describes artificial intelligence as everywhere while noting that many higher education institutions are welcoming the technology with open arms.

The article does not give specific numbers on how many students use AI, nor does it name any tools, courses or policies at the university. It does not say what the students' reactions were beyond describing them as part of the report. The piece presents the shift as a broad trend in higher education rather than a single event with a fixed date or figure. No changes to rules, requirements or budgets are described in the article.

Responsibility for the reporting rests with Nomeny, who works as a student journalist and who explained the students' embrace of AI and their reactions to its use. The article does not include direct statements from university officials, faculty or students beyond her account. No one else is named or quoted in the text provided. The context is that artificial intelligence is described as everywhere, and many higher education institutions are welcoming the advancement with open arms. stories.Headline: AI accelerators push designers to adopt vertical power delivery as currents near kiloamperes
stories.Summary:
The articles report that AI accelerators and GPUs now consume thousands of amperes at increasingly low voltages, pushing a shift to vertical power delivery that moves regulation closer to loads, as described in a November 19, 2026 semiengineering.com article. A 600W GPU running near 0.7 V forces current to rise to 1,000 amps and beyond, compounding resistive losses and voltage droop across the power delivery network. Multi-chiplet constructions compound these issues by further increasing current density and signal congestion. Designers are turning to vertical power delivery networks that relocate voltage regulator modules from the device periphery to the PCB landside, inside the accelerator package, or inside the silicon interposer. The vertical PDN trend began nearly a decade ago with backside power delivery networks on the wafer backside, enabling fine-tuned power delivery directly to transistors while reducing IR drop across tens of on-chip interconnect levels.

The articles state that backside PDNs are being extended with on-die decoupling capacitors formed in deep trenches as part of the BPDN. Recent changes inside packages, interposers, substrates, and across data center racks are becoming just as important, alongside compact passive devices like high-performance inductors. The changes involve system co-design of the PDN, interposer, power management ICs, integrated voltage regulators, DC-DC converters, capacitors, and other passives, alongside custom HPC, memory devices, and interconnects. Intel Foundry's 18A was the first to move backside wafer processing in leading-edge high-volume manufacturing, and Samsung and TSMC plan to implement backside PDNs at future advanced nodes starting next year. ASE, Marvell, Empower, and others are moving voltage regulation closer to the processor, and integration of compact passive components is becoming a key differentiator in high-density power delivery.

Nir Sever, senior director of business development at proteanTecs, said people in the most advanced semiconductors are moving from discrete PMICs to distributed IVRs placed much closer to the chip, reducing IR drop to the chip's own PDN. He said closed and fast control loops between the chip power management unit and the IVR reduce reaction time to voltage droop events from milliseconds to microseconds, allowing voltage to be tuned accurately with high granularity even on different areas of a chip. Lipen Yuan, senior director of TSMC's Advanced Technology Business Development, said during a 2024 IEDM short course that energy efficiency becomes the most important performance index for AI-infused platforms moving forward. CP Hung, vice president of corporate R&D at ASE, said AI systems are placing unprecedented demands on board-to-chip power delivery, making the final stage of voltage regulation increasingly important. Harrison Chang, vice president of corporate R&D at ASE, said power efficiency is becoming a defining challenge for next-generation AI systems, and that by shortening the high-current transmission path, the company's solution can reduce parasitic routing losses by 50% or more.

Sojan Philips, principal product manager of Redhawk-SC at Synopsys, said the move to multi-die architectures is bringing power integrity to the forefront alongside thermal, stress, and warpage challenges, but the underlying power-delivery problem already existed in advanced single-die designs. He said AI accelerators now operate at currents approaching the kiloampere range, where even milliohm-level resistance in the PDN can result in significant IR drop, and that loss of voltage margin can directly affect performance and power targets, particularly maximum operating frequency and V min. He also said backside power delivery can significantly improve power delivery by reducing IR drop and freeing frontside routing resources for signals, but it does not eliminate power-integrity challenges and changes the thermal landscape, making co-optimization of power integrity and thermal management increasingly important. Alex Kizeev, technical director of signal and power integrity at Amkor's design optimization team, said the OSAT sits where die, substrate or interposer, passives, and board meet, so OSATs are brought in earlier to model the package-level PDN and co-simulate it with the customer's die power data. Kizeev said the best results come from a PDN budget partitioned across the die, package, and board, with foundry and fabless teams owning the on-die PDN including the die power map and bump-map allocation, the substrate supplier defining stackup and via/plane technology, and the OSAT optimizing package-level pieces including stackup choice, via and ball assignment, DCap selection and placement, warpage and reliability, and validation.

The articles state that power delivery is now a significant performance limiter in data center chips, and that power delivery is becoming a system-level co-design challenge, expanding simulation needs and the role of OSATs. A simple illustration shows power efficiency dropping as the industry scales from a 1kW GPU to a 5kW GPU, with losses from the voltage regulator itself staying constant at around 13%, resistive losses jumping from 8% to 31%, and voltage droop rising from 17% to 31%. With lateral power delivery, power integrity becomes increasingly difficult to maintain as compute loads rise, and the low supply voltage of 0.7-0.9V means multiple kiloamp levels of current are needed to meet the high-power needs of modern GPUs. Fast workload transients tend to magnify voltage droop, so designers apply voltage guardbands that further increase power consumption and reduce system efficiency. For next-generation data centers built to meet AI demands, 800V DC power delivery is starting to replace traditional AC power distribution, coexisting with multiple distributed regulators located much closer to individual loads.

The articles state that next-generation PDNs begin at 800V DC and are stepped down in stages using DC-to-DC converters to 48V, 12V, and then 0.7V, for instance, with one of the most critical junctures at the point of load where integrated voltage regulators supply the AI multi-chiplet package. By limiting the number of power conversions, system-level efficiency can improve while reducing thermal cooling requirements. The voltage regulator module can be positioned underneath the PCB, a logical first step commonly referred to as vertical power delivery, while moving voltage regulation inside the main processor package and below the SoC is called integrated power delivery, and integrating voltage regulator components into the interposer itself is called fully integrated power delivery. The approach companies take depends on the company's expertise, its partners, and the complexity of the system involved. ASE is offering a range of power delivery capabilities to enable PCB backside integration, which considers the limited space inside computer trays, and its PowerSiP options can include double-sided connected capacitors sandwiched between coreless substrates, substrateless designs, solder-free cap array modules with exposed terminals for embedded substrate or PCB solutions, high-aspect-ratio 4:1 copper pin integration for lower packaging impedance, and high-density active and passive component integration using single- or double-sided molding.

stories.Headline: Researchers find thousands of uncensored AI models on major hosting platforms
stories.Summary:
Researchers from Nanyang Technological University in Singapore and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign analyzed 22,096 uncensored large language models. These researchers identified these models on five major hosting platforms to evaluate their safety and potential for producing harmful content. The study was led by Zilong Lin, who is an assistant professor of computer science at the University of Missouri-Kansas City. This team examined how these unrestrained models are shared and redistributed across the open source AI community. The resulting paper is titled Characterizing the Ecosystem of Open-Source Uncensored Large Language Models: Supply Chain, Governance, and Risks.

The study found uncensored models on US platforms Hugging Face, Kaggle, and John Snow Labs, and China platforms OpenCSG and ModelScope. These models are deployed through GitHub projects, various applications, and model routing platforms such as the service known as Open Router. The researchers noted that the number of these models rose from 100 per month in May 2023 to over 1,000 now. One specific model, dolphin-2.9.1-yi-1.5-34b, has more than 53 million downloads, including 4.8 million downloads in the last month alone. Only about 13 percent of the identified uncensored models carried any warnings regarding moderation for the users.

Zilong Lin stated that these platforms enable the sharing of artifacts, but safety alignment is difficult to assess from model files. He explained that evaluating safety requires deploying models and testing responses, which involves substantial financial and computational costs for researchers. Lin noted that models travel more easily than the information needed to assess risks, creating a significant supply chain problem. He mentioned that his team responsibly disclosed these findings to Open Router, ModelScope, OpenCSG, Kaggle, John Snow Labs, and Hugging Face. OpenCSG responded by saying the research is meaningful and supports the development of a safe and trustworthy LLM ecosystem.

The GAO found that Gemini, ChatGPT, Grok, and Claude can be coaxed to provide information for planning a terror attack. Generative AI helped enable a January 2025 Las Vegas hotel explosive device attack and a February 2026 British Columbia mass shooting. Users of certain apps may not know they are using uncensored models that lack content filtering or refusal safeguards. These models can be misused to assist with malware development or provide guidance about illegal, malicious, or manipulative activities. Twenty-seven models with 136,000 downloads showed threat indicators, including signatures associated with malware or unsafe deserialization mechanisms.

The researchers found that users apply techniques like toxic training or de-aligned training to datasets to remove refusal behavior. Examples of such models include WizardLM-7B-Uncensored and toxicqa-Llama2-13B, while Daredevil-8B-abliterated uses a newer technique called refusal-direction ablation or abliteration. This abliteration technique appeared in 2024 and quickly gained popularity, leading to a growing ecosystem of public tools within two years. Some uncensored models have legitimate uses, such as when Hugging Face used GLM-5.2 from Z.ai to analyze an infrastructure hack. Many of these uncensored models violate the licensing terms of the original models on which they were based.

Lin expects that greater verification, auditability, and transparency of models will help address the risks posed by these uncensored systems. He pointed to the Colorado AI Act and the EU AI Act, which emphasize AI documentation and the use of model cards. The researchers evaluated text output only, leaving the issues of illegal text-to-image generation, such as CSAM, beyond their study scope. It remains difficult to predict if abliteration tools will face legal challenges similar to those faced by cryptographic code in the 1990s. The articles leave open how platforms will handle the gap between model distribution and the preservation of security threat indicators.

stories.Headline: Hyundai names Park to lead vehicle platform and 42dot, adds Ma, Kim and three technical recruits
stories.Summary:
On January 13, 2026, Hyundai Motor Group named Dr. Minwoo Park as Head of the Advanced Vehicle Platform Division and CEO of 42dot, according to Hyundai's own announcement. Jeremy Ma was appointed head of Hyundai Motor Group's Silicon Valley office inside the AVP Division and concurrently serves as head of 42dot SV. Kim Dong-uk joined as Senior Executive Director after working at Tesla. 42dot recruited three named specialists: Angelo Corsaro as Senior Research Fellow, Kim Jae-young as Gleo AI Model Group Lead, and Chao Fang as SV VLA Team Lead. Follow-up reports came from outlets including BigGo Finance and Financial News.

The available record does not show that three 42dot recruits were all executives, and it does not show that all three came from Apple and NVIDIA. Park worked at NVIDIA as a vice president and led development and commercialization of autonomous-driving perception technology. Ma previously worked at Apple and NVIDIA among other organizations. Fang previously worked as a principal engineer in NVIDIA's autonomous-driving division, where he contributed to autonomous-driving foundation models and to end-to-end perception deployment. The record does not give hiring dates, pay, a headcount target, a budget or a new office address.

Hyundai's announcement said Park led development and commercialization of autonomous-driving perception technology at NVIDIA. The record describes Park's appointment as putting one person in charge of both the group's vehicle-platform engineering and its dedicated software company. Ma's dual title links the parent group's Silicon Valley presence and the software company's local team under one manager. The record says Fang will lead vision-language-action research for autonomous driving. Hyundai did not disclose Park's compensation, and no reliable source gives one.

The record says three of the six confirmed names trace back to NVIDIA, making the chipmaker the single largest talent source in the group's build-out. The record says the roles skew toward model work: perception, VLA research and an AI model group. The record says the Silicon Valley units are the physical expression of a bet that driving-AI research should sit close to where frontier models are trained. The record says the three 42dot recruits' titles read as senior technical roles, not as C-suite hires. The record says nothing found ties any of the three 42dot recruits to Apple.

The record says talent is the scarcest input in AI right now. The record refers to NVIDIA's own leadership drama, described as the Huang exit, as having already shaken the field. The record says a carmaker recruiting from the chip and compute giant's autonomous-driving ranks is buying know-how that took years to build elsewhere. The record says classic autonomy stacks split the job into separate modules for perception, prediction and planning, while VLA-style systems fold more of that pipeline into one learned model. The record says proponents say VLA handles rare situations more gracefully and skeptics worry about verifying behavior no engineer wrote down as a rule.

The record says reports tied to the latest news describe the Silicon Valley organization as expanding. The record says the leadership structure is already in place, which it calls usually the first signal that a regional hub is meant to last. The record says it leaves blank anything the available results do not establish, including hiring dates and pay. The record says it does not give a headcount target, a budget or a new office address. The record says the story is real, but the tidy three-executives-from-two-giants framing overstates it.

stories.Headline: Meta spends 78 cents of each cash dollar on AI as stock falls 21% from its high
stories.Summary:
Meta closed at $616.38 on Wednesday, 21% below its highest close of the past year of $777.59, reached on Sep 24, Trefis reported on November 19th, 2026. Meta’s ads business keeps growing, and analysts expect earnings of $34.14 a share next year, up from $29.09 this year. The size of its AI bill is holding the stock back, and unlike Amazon, Microsoft or Alphabet, Meta has no cloud business to rent that computing power to others. Meta is one of five tests for the AI trade in the Trefis series, each with a date to watch. The series starts with What 1 Big Trigger Could Make Nvidia Stock Jump By Dec 31?

Meta’s capital spending was $104.4 billion over the last year, up 66%, on data centers, servers and other long-lasting assets. It took 78 cents of every dollar of cash Meta’s business brought in, and two years ago it took 37 cents. All of it has to pay off through ads, and Meta can earn it back only one way. Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet build data centers partly to rent them to other companies, and when AI demand is strong, that rent shows up as cloud sales. Meta builds for its own apps, and its payoff has to come from better ad targeting and new products, which takes longer to show and is harder to measure.

Meta trades at 18.1 times the earnings analysts expect next year, close to Alphabet at 18.8 times. What is missing is proof that the bill will stop growing faster than the business. Meta is already 21% below its high while investors wait for that proof. For every dollar its benchmark lost, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio lost about 81 cents on average, holding 30 quality stocks in equal weight. The source is Trefis, using Morningstar data, with each row covering the four quarters to September.

Dec 9 brings the Fed, and a rate hike is widely expected, which makes spending that pays off years from now harder to justify. Late January brings Meta’s next report, expected then, and two numbers to watch are the 2027 spending plan and growth in ad sales. If spending rises less than ads, the worry should ease, and if spending jumps again while ad growth stays flat, the worry should deepen. Early February brings Alphabet and Amazon, whose spending plans set the tone for all of big tech, and their ad businesses are also the closest match to Meta’s.

Alphabet’s side is in Why Is Alphabet Stock Down 30%? If Meta is a large part of what you own, one company’s spending choice decides a lot of your result, which is a good reason to think now about how and when you would sell. If Meta is a big part of your wealth, so are its risk and its tax bill. Our partner advisory firm offers a free 30-minute strategy review covering a floor under losses and a lower-tax way out.

The article is for education, not a recommendation to buy or sell. For questions about the article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com. In Trefis’s view, the gap between spending growth and ad growth will decide where the stock goes. The article leaves open what Meta’s 2027 spending plan will be and how much ad sales will grow.

It leaves open what the Fed will do on Dec 9 beyond the widely expected rate hike. It leaves open what Alphabet and Amazon will plan for spending in early February. It leaves open how and when a holder would sell. More to follow.

stories.Headline: AI infrastructure drives electronics assembly market toward $4 trillion by 2030, association reports
stories.Summary:
The global market for electronics assembly will grow to more than USD 4 trillion by 2030, according to the Global Electronics Association, which published the figure in its 2026 Global Electronics Assembly Report. The market was worth USD 2,124.5 billion in 2025 and will reach USD 4,037.8 billion in 2030, almost twice as much, corresponding to average annual growth of 13.7%. The report covers EMS providers and ODMs as well as brand owners that assemble products in their own factories. Cloud and AI infrastructure accounts for more than 60% of the expected growth. Cloud and AI infrastructure accounted for 20.5% of the market in 2025, only just ahead of communications at 20.2%, and by 2030 its share will have doubled to 40%, with the segment expected to account for 62% of the market's total growth.

The segment will almost double in a single year, from USD 435.9 billion in 2025 to USD 857.1 billion in 2026, after which the pace slows, and between 2029 and 2030 it grows by only around 2%. By 2030 it will be worth USD 1,626.4 billion, almost four times as much as in 2025. Other segments grow far more slowly over the whole period, ranging from 4.5% a year for consumer electronics to 9.8% for industrial electronics. Thiago Guimaraes, director of industry intelligence for the Association, said the AI infrastructure buildout continues to drive the bulk of the electronics manufacturing growth through 2030. He said accelerated servers require more processing, memory, power and interconnect hardware, increasing the value of each system and creating more manufacturing opportunities for the boards and other assemblies that go into them.

The EMS and ODM market is highly concentrated, with the three largest providers accounting for 41% of global revenue, according to the report. Asia-Pacific holds a majority of the market in seven of the nine segments, and the largest share in the remaining two. Christoph Solka, the association's other director of industry intelligence, still sees room for smaller players, saying projected growth is so strong that there is still opportunity for the more than 7,500 other players. The association's report sets out the forecast through 2030. Evertiq Expo Vienna takes place on January 28, followed by Evertiq Expo Grenoble on March 4, both bringing together industry professionals to exchange knowledge, explore new developments and build business connections.

stories.Headline: Rivian announces second Autonomy & AI Day for 9 December in Palo Alto
stories.Summary:
Rivian will hold its second Autonomy & AI Day on 9 December, the electric vehicle maker has announced, with the event livestreamed from Palo Alto at 10:00 PT. At the event the company is expected to set out progress on point-to-point assisted driving and on the hardware that will support hands-off and eyes-off capability on upcoming models. The agenda centres on Rivian's end-to-end self-driving system, including its onboard inference platform, which is capable of 200 trillion operations per second. Rivian is also expected to outline its sensor roadmap, including cameras, radar and next-generation lidar, for future vehicles such as the R2 and R3.

The day will cover the Autonomy+ Early Access Program, which lets select subscribers test point-to-point driving ahead of a broader rollout planned for 2027. Rivian will highlight progress in 3D scene simulation, synthetic data and vision-based foundation models following its acquisition of Third Dimension AI, alongside demonstrations of upcoming over-the-air software updates and in-cabin AI features. The company has also promised announcements on strategic partners for silicon design and software integration. Rivian's 2027 timeline puts it alongside Mercedes-Benz, which brings point-to-point assistance to the US next year, and behind Tesla, which already offers supervised point-to-point driving.

The promised silicon and software partnerships are the most important part of the day, according to the article, since they will decide how cheaply Rivian can bring the feature to the lower-priced R2. The article does not name the partners Rivian will announce, and it gives no further detail on what the partnerships will involve. It also does not say what the over-the-air updates will contain or when they will reach vehicles. The event itself is the next scheduled step, with the livestream from Palo Alto at 10:00 PT on 9 December.

stories.Headline: Nothing shows its screenless AI device and CEO Carl Pei says it ships in December 2026
stories.Summary:
Nothing showed the first look at its screenless AI device on November 19, 2026, and the internet immediately saw a voice recorder. The product has a brushed-metal body, rounded corners, one large central button and two small lights. India Today described the design as resembling a voice recorder. Nothing itself has not said that, and it has named no price, no spec sheet and no product name. Founder and CEO Carl Pei said it is the company's first "AI-native product."

Nothing has confirmed the product will launch or begin shipping in December 2026, and the company's own wording says the product ships next month. Nothing has not announced a price, has not published technical specifications, has not confirmed which countries will get the product at launch and has not revealed an official name. Nothing also has not confirmed voice recording, ambient listening, note-taking or conversation capture. As of November 19, 2026, none of the seven open questions listed in earlier coverage on this site have been answered by Nothing in public. The confirmed list is short: the first AI-native product label, no screen, the design as shown and the December 2026 window.

Pei said on the record that "Context doesn't live in a chat box." He also said, "Our first AI-native product ships next month. No new screen. Couldn't have been an app." The chat-box line is a criticism of how most people use AI today, because typing a question into a text window forces users to supply context by hand.

The second quote makes three claims: the product ships next month, it adds no new screen and it could not have been an app. Neither quote mentions recording, microphones or voice. India Today framed the reveal around one comparison, saying the device looks like a voice recorder based on the design Nothing shared before launch. Some commentators read a red marking in the teaser as a recording indicator, but that reading is unconfirmed. Nothing has not said the large button starts a recording, has not said the red element signals one and has not said the device carries an AI voice agent.

The reveal lands in a crowded week for AI hardware and agents, with rivals shipping glasses, phone makers pushing assistants and operating systems adding guardrails for agent software. Buyers and developers are affected because the product category itself is still undefined in public. Over the past few years, startups and established brands have tried pins, handheld assistants, pendants and glasses, and reviewers were often harsh. The recurring complaint was that a phone already did the job, and the new device added a second thing to charge and carry without a clear payoff.

The lesson from that wave is that a dedicated AI device survives only if it does one thing noticeably better than a phone app. Pei's statement that the product could not have been an app reads like a direct response to that history. Several earlier products faced backlash because marketing promised a general assistant. Nothing has not said which AI models power the device or where processing happens, whether on the hardware, on a paired phone or in the cloud.

Reviewers will test the claim in December, and they will ask the same question every time: why not just use the phone? Nothing has not explained what the brushed-metal body, rounded corners, single large central button or two small lights do. The two small lights will define how trustworthy the device feels, and that matters more for a product that may be near conversations or private moments. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Anthropic shares plunge 11% as AI trade unravels and S&P 500 enters correction
stories.Summary:
A bruising tech rout roiled global markets on November 20, 2026, as investors piled into bonds. The unraveling of the artificial intelligence trade drove the S&P 500 down 10 percent from its peak. This decline matches the technical definition of a correction and marks a long slide for US stocks. The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5 percent during this period of market instability. Anthropic PBC saw its shares plunge 11 percent on its second day of trading.

The S&P 500 broke below its 200 day moving average and now sits near a structural floor. Emerging market shares extended a drop from a record to 20 percent while the dollar sought a fourth weekly gain. Investors moved toward haven assets including Treasuries and defensive shares as volatility surged. Stability for the S&P 500 will depend on holding key support near the 7,000 level. The market is now reacting to the conclusion of the record IPO for Anthropic PBC.

Adam Turnquist of LPL Financial said that a perceived risk clearing event failed to revive the general risk appetite. He noted that enthusiasm for the Anthropic IPO did not spill over because AI cycle concerns lingered. Turnquist also stated that technical damage is mounting for the broader market. He believes that stability in the AI trade is a vital factor for a durable recovery. These comments highlight the shift from exuberance to mounting doubts over the AI trade.

Chris Senyek at Wolfe Research said stocks are likely biased to the downside until technical indicators are washed out. He noted that AI worries, Fed policy, and inflation remain key overhangs absent an Iran peace deal. Mark Hackett at Nationwide suggested that a capitulatory washout could ultimately prove constructive for the market. He believes a true flush may reset positioning and sentiment for a sustainable rally. These analysts suggest that tech valuations and geopolitical turmoil are affecting investor confidence.

The AI trade grew explosively before this rout, but investors now question if vast spending can be sustained. Regulation is expected to tighten while the Federal Reserve is widely expected to raise interest rates. The Anthropic IPO initially consumed investor attention, with supply chain stocks moving on pricing and deal size. This event capped a growth period for the startup that was filled with contradictions. The current slide is the longest for US stocks since the year 2020.

Chart watchers are now looking for clues to determine if the worst of the rout is over. The market faces a choice between a rebound and a deeper pullback before the year ends. It remains unclear if the current volatility will lead to a sustainable rally or further declines. The impact of future Federal Reserve rate hikes on tech valuations is not yet determined. Whether a peace deal in Iran will occur to ease equity overhangs remains an open question.

stories.Headline: ZData and NTT Data build Johor data centre campus as residents protest
stories.Summary:
ZData and NTT Data are building a data centre campus in Gelang Patah, Johor. This construction began on Bukit Resam, a hill that was partially deforested for the project. Residents of nearby housing estates protested the site in February to stop dust pollution. They also demanded compensation for potential health impacts caused by the construction activities. These protests were reportedly the first of their kind against a data centre in Malaysia.

The 43 hectare campus includes a 15.6 hectare facility for ZData and 27.7 hectares for NTT Data. ZData acquired its land from the developer Tropicana Firstwide for its first Southeast Asian facility. There are over 70 projects approved or planned across Johor, according to Baxtel research. At least 17 parks are operating or under construction in the Iskandar Puteri area. The project site covers 64.9 hectares including access roads and infrastructure.

ZData stated it uses reclaimed water from an on-site plant instead of municipal water. The company plans to procure 630,000 megawatt-hours of renewable electricity annually from two local firms. ZData claims its building materials and cooling systems are designed to reduce localised heat. It says its facility is the first in Malaysia to receive a provisional GreenRE Platinum rating. ZData also claimed that construction activities contributing to dust pollution were currently minimal.

Ulaganathan Krishnan said the community lost its way of life to a project that does not benefit them. A local farmer noted that his chicks began hatching at unusual times since the forest clearing. Some residents expressed enthusiasm for the investment and jobs the data centres might bring. Greenpeace Malaysia called for a ban on data centres located near residential areas. Residents of Setia Eco Gardens reported seeing critically endangered Raffles banded langurs on the site.

The project followed a December 2021 environmental impact assessment conducted by Tropicana Firstwide. This survey found only common mammals like rats and squirrels on the total plot. The Johor office of the Department of Environment approved the assessment and the site clearing. The government halted expansion of water intensive cooling systems in November 2025 until mid 2027. It also stopped approving new tier 1 and tier 2 centres that use high water volumes.

The government introduced a tariff to encourage operators to reuse water for their facilities. National utility plans include adding 11.8 gigawatts of new power capacity by 2033 using gas plants. Greenpeace Malaysia wants the government to require more detailed Schedule 2 environmental impact assessments. The Department of Environment did not provide a copy of the project assessment by press time. NTT Data did not respond to queries about the environmental and social impact of the campus.
